title.zh: 卷五 魏書五 后妃傳
title.en: Volume 5: Book of Wei 5: Biographies of Empresses and Concubines
title.raw: 卷五 魏書五 后妃傳 Volume 5: Book of Wei 5: Biographies of Empresses and Concubines

sentences.zh: 易稱「男正位乎外，女正位乎內；

translations.literal: The Changes says, "The man takes the correct position outside, the woman takes the correct position inside;
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "The man takes the correct position outside, the woman takes the correct position inside;

sentences.zh: 男女正，天地之大義也」。

translations.literal: when man and woman are correct, it is the great righteousness of heaven and earth."
translations.idiomatic: when each stands in the right relation, that is the great moral order of heaven and earth."

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，莫不明后妃之制，順天地之德，故二妃嬪媯，虞道克隆，任、姒配姬，周室用熈，廢興存亡，恆此之由。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings all clarified the regulations for empresses and consorts and complied with the virtue of heaven and earth; therefore the two consorts married into the Gui clan, and the way of Yu flourished; Ren and Si were paired with the Ji house, and the Zhou house thereby prospered—rise and fall, survival and perdition constantly stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: Every wise king of antiquity made clear the rules governing empresses and concubines and aligned them with the moral pattern of heaven and earth. Hence the two royal brides who joined the Gui line made Yao’s line thrive, while Ren and Si, wed into the Ji clan, brought radiance to Zhou. Whether a state flourishes or fails has almost always turned on this.

sentences.zh: 春秋說云天子十二女，諸侯九女，考之情理，不易之典也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn exegesis says the Son of Heaven has twelve women and a feudal lord nine women; examined against human reason, this is an unchanging norm.
translations.idiomatic: Exegetical tradition on the Spring and Autumn Annals assigns twelve consorts to the Son of Heaven and nine to a feudal lord; weighed by common sense, that norm has not changed.

sentences.zh: 而末世奢縱，肆其侈欲，至使男女怨曠，感動和氣，惟色是崇，不本淑懿，故風教陵遲而大綱毀泯，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet in degenerate ages men grew extravagant and unrestrained, indulging their lavish desires until men and women were left resentful and long separated, disturbing the harmonious qi; they honored only physical beauty and did not root conduct in virtuous grace, so customs and instruction declined and the great bonds were ruined and lost—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, however, rulers gave themselves to excess and appetite until men and women languished apart in bitterness, unsettling the harmonious air of the realm. They exalted mere loveliness instead of grounding choice in true goodness, until morals frayed and the fundamental ties of society collapsed. What a waste.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，有國有家者，其可以永鑒矣！

translations.literal: Alas—those who possess a state or a family may take this as a mirror forever!
translations.idiomatic: Alas: any who would hold a realm or a household ought to keep this lesson before them always.

sentences.zh: 漢制，帝祖母曰太皇太后，帝母曰皇太后，帝妃曰皇后，其餘內官十有四等。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations the emperor’s grandmother was called Grand Empress Dowager, the emperor’s mother Empress Dowager, the emperor’s consort Empress, and the remaining inner-palace offices numbered fourteen ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Han law styled the sovereign’s grandmother Grand Empress Dowager, his mother Empress Dowager, his chief consort Empress, and recognized fourteen grades of inner-court women below them.

sentences.zh: 魏因漢法，母后之號皆如舊制，自夫人以下，世有增損。

translations.literal: Wei followed Han law; titles for the empress dowager and the like all matched the old system; from the rank of Lady downward, each generation saw additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: Wei adopted Han precedent: the titles of the empress’s mother and similar ranks stayed as before, while from Lady downward successive reigns added or pruned offices.

sentences.zh: 太祖建國，始命王后，其下五等：有夫人，有昭儀，有倢伃，有容華，有美人。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor founded the state he first appointed a queen; below her were five grades: there was Lady, there was Brilliant Companion, there was Handmaid of Favor, there was Graceful Splendor, and there was Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao established his kingdom he first set a queen above five grades: Lady, Brilliant Companion, Handmaid of Favor, Graceful Splendor, and Beauty.

sentences.zh: 文帝增貴嬪、淑媛、脩容、順成、良人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen added Honored Concubine, Virtuous Lady, Cultivated Countenance, Accomplished Success, and Good Woman.
translations.idiomatic: Wen-di expanded the roster with Honored Concubine, Virtuous Lady, Cultivated Countenance, Accomplished Success, and Good Woman.

sentences.zh: 明帝增淑妃、昭華、脩儀；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming added Virtuous Consort, Splendid Companion, and Cultivated Deportment;
translations.idiomatic: Ming-di added Virtuous Consort, Splendid Companion, and Cultured Bearing;

sentences.zh: 除順成官。

translations.literal: he abolished the office of Accomplished Success.
translations.idiomatic: and he abolished the Accomplished Success post.

sentences.zh: 太和中始復命夫人，登其位於淑妃之上。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he again ordered the rank of Lady and placed it above Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe the court restored the title Lady and set it above Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 自夫人以下爵凡十二等：貴嬪、夫人，位次皇后，爵無所視；

translations.literal: From Lady downward the noble ranks totaled twelve grades: Honored Concubine and Lady ranked next after the queen and had no parallel for their noble rank;
translations.idiomatic: Below the empress came twelve noble grades. Honored Concubine and Lady stood immediately beneath her, with no exact analogue among outside nobility;

sentences.zh: 淑妃位視相國，爵比諸侯王；

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort’s position was equated to the Chancellor and her noble rank compared to a feudal prince;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort’s salary matched the Chancellor’s and her fief ranked with a prince of the blood;

sentences.zh: 淑媛位視御史大夫，爵比縣公；

translations.literal: Virtuous Lady’s position was equated to the Imperial Counselor and her noble rank compared to a county duke;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Lady matched the Imperial Counselor and ranked with a county duke;

sentences.zh: 昭儀比縣侯；

translations.literal: Brilliant Companion was compared to a county marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant Companion matched a county marquis;

sentences.zh: 昭華比鄉侯；

translations.literal: Splendid Companion was compared to a village marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Splendid Companion matched a village marquis;

sentences.zh: 脩容比亭侯；

translations.literal: Cultivated Countenance was compared to a pavilion marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Cultivated Countenance matched a pavilion marquis;

sentences.zh: 脩儀比關內侯；

translations.literal: Cultivated Deportment was compared to a marquis within the passes;
translations.idiomatic: Cultured Bearing matched a marquis-within-the-passes;

sentences.zh: 倢伃視中二千石；

translations.literal: Handmaid of Favor was equated to two thousand shi at the full rate;
translations.idiomatic: Handmaid of Favor drew pay like a full two-thousand-shi official;

sentences.zh: 容華視真二千石；

translations.literal: Graceful Splendor was equated to two thousand shi at the true rate;
translations.idiomatic: Graceful Splendor drew true two-thousand-shi rank;

sentences.zh: 美人視比二千石；

translations.literal: Beauty was equated to two thousand shi by comparison;
translations.idiomatic: Beauty compared to two-thousand-shi salary;

sentences.zh: 良人視千石。

translations.literal: Good Woman was equated to one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Good Woman matched one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 武宣卞皇后

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan of the martial and manifest virtue, née Bian
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan (the martial and manifest empress), surnamed Bian

sentences.zh: 武宣卞皇后，琅邪開陽人，文帝母也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, née Bian, was a native of Kaiyang in Langye and was Emperor Wen’s mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bian, posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, came from Kaiyang in Langye and was Cao Pi’s mother.

sentences.zh: 本倡家，

translations.literal: Her family had been entertainers by profession.
translations.idiomatic: She was born into a family of performers.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：后以漢延熹三年十二月己巳生齊郡白亭，有黃氣滿室移日。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: The empress was born on the jisi day of the twelfth month of the third year of Han’s Yanxi era at White Pavilion in Qi commandery, and yellow qi filled the chamber for a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Book of Wei records that she was born on jisi in the twelfth month of Han Yanxi 3 at White Pavilion in Qi, while yellow vapor filled the room for an entire day.

sentences.zh: 父敬侯怪之，以問卜者王旦，旦曰：「此吉祥也。」〉

translations.literal: Her father the Marquis of Respect wondered at it and asked the diviner Wang Dan, who said, "This is auspicious."〉
translations.idiomatic: Her father, ennobled as the Respectful Marquis, was troubled and questioned the diviner Wang Dan, who answered, “This is a blessed omen.”〉

sentences.zh: 年二十，太祖於譙納后爲妾。

translations.literal: At age twenty the Grand Progenitor took her as a concubine at Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: When she was twenty, Cao Cao took her as a concubine at Qiao.

sentences.zh: 後隨太祖至洛。

translations.literal: Later she followed the Grand Progenitor to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: She later accompanied him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及董卓爲亂，太祖微服東出避難。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo threw the realm into chaos the Grand Progenitor went out east in disguise to escape danger.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo’s rebellion convulsed the capital, Cao Cao slipped away in plain clothes toward the east.

sentences.zh: 袁術傳太祖凶問，時太祖左右至洛者皆欲歸，后止之曰：「曹君吉凶未可知，今日還家，明日若在，何靣目復相見也？

translations.literal: Yuan Shu spread word that the Grand Progenitor had died; those of his attendants who had reached Luoyang all wished to return, but the empress stopped them, saying, "We do not yet know whether Lord Cao is alive or dead; if we go home today and he is alive tomorrow, with what face could we meet him again?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu circulated a false report of Cao Cao’s death. His followers in Luoyang wanted to flee homeward, but Lady Bian told them, “You cannot know yet whether my lord lives or dies. If you leave today and he proves alive tomorrow, how could you bear to look him in the eye?

sentences.zh: 正使禍至，共死何苦！」

translations.literal: Even if disaster comes, what hardship is there in dying together!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if the worst comes, is dying together so terrible?”

sentences.zh: 遂從后言。

translations.literal: So they followed the empress’s words.
translations.idiomatic: They stayed because she said so.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而善之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor heard of it he praised her.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao heard the story and approved her steadiness.

sentences.zh: 建安初，丁夫人廢，遂以后爲繼室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jian’an era Lady Ding was set aside, and he then made the empress his successor wife.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jian’an, after Lady Ding was cast off, he made Lady Bian his principal wife.

sentences.zh: 諸子無母者，太祖皆令后養之。

translations.literal: For sons who lacked mothers the Grand Progenitor ordered the empress to rear them all.
translations.idiomatic: He told her to raise every motherless son of his household.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太祖始有丁夫人，又劉夫人生子脩及清河長公主。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary states: At first the Grand Progenitor had Lady Ding, and Lady Liu bore sons Xiu and the Princess of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Summary adds that Cao Cao first had Lady Ding, while Lady Liu bore Cao Ang and the Princess of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 劉早終，丁養子脩。

translations.literal: Lady Liu died early, and Lady Ding raised son Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu died young, and Lady Ding reared Cao Ang as her own.

sentences.zh: 子脩亡於穰，丁常言：「將我兒殺之，都不復念！」

translations.literal: When son Xiu perished at Rang, Lady Ding kept saying, "You killed my son; you never think of me again!"
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Ang died at Rang, Lady Ding cried again and again, “You got my son killed and spare me no thought at all!”

sentences.zh: 遂哭泣無節。

translations.literal: Then she wept without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: and she wept without measure.

sentences.zh: 太祖忿之，遣歸家，欲其意折。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor grew angry, sent her home, and intended her resolve to break.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Cao Cao sent her back to her family, expecting her resolve to crumble.

sentences.zh: 後太祖就見之，夫人方織，外人傳云「公至」，夫人踞機如故。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Progenitor went to see her; the lady was weaving, and when outsiders announced "The lord has come" she sat astride the loom as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cao Cao went to see her. She was at her loom, and when someone outside announced, "The lord has arrived," she remained seated at the loom as before.

sentences.zh: 太祖到，撫其背曰：「顧我共載歸乎！」

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor arrived he stroked her back and said, "Will you not ride home with me!"
translations.idiomatic: He stepped in, laid a hand on her back, and said, “Won’t you come home with me in the carriage?”

sentences.zh: 夫人不顧，又不應。

translations.literal: The lady did not turn her head and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: She neither looked at him nor replied.

sentences.zh: 太祖却行，立於戶外，復云：「得無尚可邪！」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor stepped backward, stood outside the door, and said again, "Could it still be all right!"
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to the threshold and called, “Is there still no way to patch this?”

sentences.zh: 遂不應，太祖曰：「真訣矣。」

translations.literal: Still she did not answer, and the Grand Progenitor said, "It is truly over."
translations.idiomatic: Again she was silent, and he said, “Then it is finished between us.”

sentences.zh: 遂與絕，欲其家嫁之，其家不敢。

translations.literal: He broke with her and wished her family to marry her off, but her family did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: He severed ties and wanted her kin to remarry her, yet they dared not.

sentences.zh: 初，丁夫人旣爲嫡，加有子脩，丁視后母子不足。

translations.literal: At first, once Lady Ding had been principal wife and moreover had son Xiu, Lady Ding regarded the empress and her children as beneath notice.
translations.idiomatic: While Lady Ding was still principal consort and mother to Cao Ang, she looked down on Lady Bian and her sons.

sentences.zh: 后爲繼室，不念舊惡，因太祖出行，常四時使人饋遺，又私迎之，延以正坐而己下之，迎來送去，有如昔日。

translations.literal: After the empress became successor wife she did not remember old wrongs; whenever the Grand Progenitor traveled she regularly sent seasonal gifts in all four seasons, and also privately welcomed her, seated her in the seat of honor while placing herself below, escorting her coming and going as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lady Bian became principal wife she refused to nurse old grudges. Whenever Cao Cao was away she sent seasonal gifts, received Lady Ding in private, gave her the host’s seat while taking a lower place herself, and saw her off and welcomed her as in earlier times.

sentences.zh: 丁謝曰：「廢放之人，夫人何能常爾邪！」

translations.literal: Lady Ding declined, saying, "I am a cast-off person—how can you always treat me thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding protested, “I am a discarded woman—why should you honor me like this?”

sentences.zh: 其後丁亡，后請太祖殯葬，許之，乃葬許城南。

translations.literal: Later when Lady Ding died the empress asked the Grand Progenitor for a funeral; he granted it, and she was buried south of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Ding died, Lady Bian begged Cao Cao to bury her properly; he agreed, and she was interred south of Xu.

sentences.zh: 後太祖病困，自慮不起，歎曰：「我前後行意，於心未曾有所負也。

translations.literal: Later, when the Grand Progenitor was gravely ill and feared he would not recover, he sighed, "In all I have done before and after, my heart has never knowingly wronged anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Cao Cao lay dying, he sighed, “In everything I have done I do not believe I ever knowingly betrayed another.

sentences.zh: 假令死而有靈，子脩若問『我母所在』，我將何辭以荅！」

translations.literal: Suppose that after death there is awareness and son Xiu asks, 'Where is my mother?'—what words could I use to answer!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the dead have awareness and Cao Ang asks where his mother is, what answer could I give?”

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：后性約儉，不尚華麗，無文繡珠玉，器皆黑漆。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: The empress’s nature was frugal and restrained; she did not esteem splendor and finery; there were no patterned silks or pearls and jade; vessels were all black lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei adds that Lady Bian lived plainly—no embroidered silks or jade ornaments, only black-lacquer ware.

sentences.zh: 太祖常得名璫數具，命后自選一具，后取其中者，太祖問其故，對曰：「取其上者爲貪，取其下者爲偽，故取其中者。」〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once obtained several fine pearl hairpins and ordered the empress to choose one; she took those of middle quality, and when the Grand Progenitor asked the reason she replied, "To take the best would be greed; to take the lowest would be pretense; therefore I take the middle ones."〉
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao offered her a choice of jeweled pins she picked middling ones, explaining, “The finest would show greed, the poorest affectation; the middle course is honest.”〉

sentences.zh: 文帝爲太子，左右長御賀后曰：「將軍拜太子，天下莫不歡喜，后當傾府藏賞賜。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was heir apparent, the chief women attendants congratulated the empress, saying, "The general has been invested as heir; none under heaven fails to rejoice—the empress ought to empty the treasury stores to reward and bestow."
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi became heir, his senior maids told Lady Bian, “The heir has been named; the whole realm rejoices. You should fling open the treasuries and give largesse.”

sentences.zh: 后曰：「王自以丕年大，故用爲嗣，我但當以免無教導之過爲幸耳，亦何爲當重賜遺乎！」

translations.literal: The empress said, "The king appointed Pi heir because of his age; I should count myself fortunate merely to escape blame for failing to instruct him—why should there be heavy gifts and largesse!"
translations.idiomatic: She answered, “The king chose Pi because he is the elder son. I am lucky enough not to be faulted for poor upbringing—why heap rewards on everyone?”

sentences.zh: 長御還，具以語太祖。

translations.literal: The chief attendants returned and reported everything to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: They reported her words to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖恱曰：「怒不變容，喜不失節，故是最爲難。」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said, "Not to change countenance in anger nor lose measure in joy—therein lies what is hardest."
translations.idiomatic: He said with satisfaction, “To stay calm in anger and measured in joy—that is the rarest thing of all.”

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜爲王后，策曰：「夫人卞氏，撫養諸子，有母儀之德。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year she was invested as queen; the patent read, "Lady Bian has reared the various sons and possesses the virtue of a motherly model.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian’an she was enfeoffed as queen. The edict read, “Lady Bian has nurtured the princes and embodies a mother’s standard.

sentences.zh: 今進位王后，太子諸侯陪位，羣卿上壽，減國內死罪一等。」

translations.literal: Now we advance her to queen; the heir apparent and feudal lords shall attend in support, the ministers shall offer longevity toasts, and capital crimes within the realm are reduced one grade."
translations.idiomatic: We therefore raise her to queen; the heir and feudal lords shall attend while ministers toast her long life, and death sentences across the domain are commuted one degree.”

sentences.zh: 二十五年，太祖崩，文帝即王位，尊后曰王太后，及踐阼，尊后曰皇太后，稱永壽宮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Grand Progenitor died; Emperor Wen assumed the king’s position, honored the empress as Queen Dowager, and when he ascended the throne honored her as Empress Dowager, with her residence called Yongshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Cao Cao died. Cao Pi, now king, styled her Queen Dowager, and as emperor raised her to Empress Dowager of Yongshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：后以國用不足，滅損御食，諸金銀器物皆去之。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: Because state funds were insufficient the empress reduced palace meals and removed all gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Book of Wei notes that she cut palace meals when the treasury ran short and stripped the kitchens of gold and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 東阿王植，太后少子，最愛之。

translations.literal: Prince of Dong'e Zhi was the empress dowager’s youngest son and the one she loved most.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi, prince of Dong’e, was her youngest and her favorite.

sentences.zh: 後植犯法，爲有司所奏，文帝令太后弟子奉車都尉蘭持公卿議白太后，太后曰：「不意此兒所作如是，汝還語帝，不可以我故壞國法。」

translations.literal: Later when Zhi violated the law and was impeached by the responsible officials, Emperor Wen ordered the empress dowager’s nephew Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Lan to present the deliberations of the dukes and ministers to the empress dowager; the empress dowager said, "I never expected this child to act thus; you return and tell the emperor that he must not, for my sake, damage the laws of the state."
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Zhi broke the law and officials impeached him, Wen-di sent her nephew Lan, commandant of the imperial carriage, with the ministers’ verdict. She said only, “I never thought this boy would go so far. Go back and tell the Son of Heaven not to bend the statutes for my sake.”

sentences.zh: 及自見帝，不以爲言。

translations.literal: When she herself saw the emperor she did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: When she next saw the emperor she never raised the matter.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：文帝夢磨錢，欲使文滅而更愈明，以問周宣。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: Emperor Wen dreamed of grinding cash, wishing the inscription to wear away yet it grew clearer; he asked Zhou Xuan about it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks: Wen-di dreamed of grinding coins, wanting the characters to fade yet they grew sharper, and asked Zhou Xuan.

sentences.zh: 宣荅曰：「此陛下家事，雖意欲爾，而太后不聽。」

translations.literal: Xuan replied, "This is a household matter of Your Majesty; though you may wish it so, the empress dowager will not listen."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuan answered, “This concerns your own household: though you wish one outcome, the empress dowager will not consent.”

sentences.zh: 則太后用意，不得如此書所言也。

translations.literal: Then the empress dowager’s intent cannot have been as this text describes.
translations.idiomatic: So her attitude cannot have matched what this passage claims.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》又曰：太后每隨軍征行，見高年白首，輙住車呼問，賜與絹帛，對之涕泣曰：「恨父母不及我時也。」

translations.literal: The Book of Wei also states: Whenever the empress dowager followed the army on campaign and saw white-haired elders she would halt the carriage, call out to ask after them, and grant silk and cloth; facing them with tears she said, "I regret that my parents did not reach my time."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei also says that on campaign she stopped her carriage for white-haired villagers, gave them silk, and wept, “I mourn that my own parents never lived to see days like these.”

sentences.zh: 太后每見外親，不假以顏色，常言「居處當務節儉，不當望賞賜，念自佚也。

translations.literal: Whenever the empress dowager saw outer kin she did not relax her stern countenance and often said, "In dwelling one must practice frugality; one should not expect rewards and largesse or think only of ease.
translations.idiomatic: To kinsmen from outside the palace she showed no easy warmth, warning, “Live modestly; do not look for gifts or live only for comfort.

sentences.zh: 外舍當怪吾遇之太薄，吾自有常度故也。

translations.literal: Those outside will surely wonder that I treat them too coldly—I have my constant measure for it.
translations.idiomatic: They may think me harsh, but I keep to my rule.

sentences.zh: 吾事武帝四五十年，行儉日久，不能自變爲奢，有犯科禁者，吾且能加罪一等耳，莫望錢米恩貸也。」

translations.literal: I have served Emperor Wu four or five decades and have long practiced austerity; I cannot suddenly turn extravagant; if anyone breaks the statutes I can only add one degree to the penalty—do not expect cash or grain indulgence from me."
translations.idiomatic: I served Emperor Wu forty or fifty years in frugal habit; I will not turn lavish now. Whoever breaks the law gets an extra degree of punishment from me—never expect money or grain favors.”

sentences.zh: 帝爲太后弟秉起第，第成，太后幸第請諸家外親，設下廚，無異膳。

translations.literal: The emperor built a mansion for the empress dowager’s younger brother Bing; when it was finished the empress dowager visited the mansion and invited the various outer kin, setting out a lower kitchen with no unusual delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built a mansion for her brother Bing; when she toured it she feasted the kin with plain fare from the lower kitchen, nothing special.

sentences.zh: 太后左右菜食粟飯，無魚肉。

translations.literal: Those to the empress dowager’s left and right ate vegetable fare and millet rice, with no fish or meat.
translations.idiomatic: Her own attendants ate vegetables and millet, no meat or fish.

sentences.zh: 其儉如此。〉

translations.literal: Her frugality was thus.〉
translations.idiomatic: Such was her austerity.〉

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，尊太后曰太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne he honored the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming-di succeeded he raised her to Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，文帝欲追封太后父母，尚書陳羣奏曰：「陛下以聖德應運受命，創業革制，當永爲後式。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era Emperor Wen wished posthumously to enfeoff the empress dowager’s parents; Minister of the Secretariat Chen Qun submitted, "Your Majesty, endowed with sagely virtue, has received the mandate, founded the enterprise, and reformed institutions; you should forever be a model for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu, Wen-di wanted to posthumously ennoble Lady Bian’s parents. Chen Qun objected: “You received the mandate with sage virtue and set new institutions—you must be the pattern for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 案典籍之文，無婦人分土命爵之制。

translations.literal: Examining the texts of the canons, there is no system by which a woman is granted land or a noble title.
translations.idiomatic: The classics nowhere grant women fiefs or noble rank of their own.

sentences.zh: 在禮典，婦因夫爵。

translations.literal: In the ritual canons a woman takes rank through her husband.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual gives a wife rank only through her husband.

sentences.zh: 秦違古法，漢氏因之，非先王之令典也。」

translations.literal: Qin violated the ancient pattern; Han continued it—it is not the canonical model of the former kings."
translations.idiomatic: Qin broke the ancient rule and Han followed suit; neither matches the true kings’ code.”

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此議是也，其勿施行。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This opinion is correct; do not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed: “Do not enact it.

sentences.zh: 以作著詔下藏之臺閣，永爲後式。」

translations.literal: Draw up an edict recording this, deposit it in the archives, and let it be a model forever."
translations.idiomatic: Instead promulgate an edict, file it in the tower archives, and let it stand forever as precedent.”

sentences.zh: 至太和四年春，明帝乃追謚太后祖父廣曰開陽恭侯，父遠曰敬侯，祖母周封陽都君及敬侯夫人，皆贈印綬。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Taihe Emperor Ming posthumously honored the empress dowager’s grandfather Guang as Marquis Gong of Kaiyang, her father Yuan as Marquis Jing, her grandmother Zhou as Mistress of Yangdu and the Lady of Marquis Jing, all with seals and ribbons conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4 Ming-di belatedly ennobled her grandfather Guang as Marquis Gong of Kaiyang, her father Yuan as Marquis Jing, and her grandmother Zhou as lady of Yangdu and consort of Marquis Jing, each with seals and cords.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，后崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: She died that fifth month.

sentences.zh: 七月，合葬高陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month she was jointly buried at Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month she was laid beside Cao Cao in the Gaoling mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 初，太后弟秉，以功封都鄉侯，黃初七年進封開陽侯，邑千二百戶，爲昭烈將軍。

translations.literal: At first, the empress dowager's younger brother Bing, for merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Capital Village; in the seventh year of Huangchu he was advanced to Marquis of Kaiyang with a fief of one thousand two hundred households and made General Who Displays Fierce Valor.
translations.idiomatic: At first the empress dowager's younger brother Bing was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Capital Village for his service. In Huangchu 7 he was promoted to Marquis of Kaiyang with a fief of twelve hundred households and made General Who Displays Fierce Valor.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：初，卞后弟秉，當建安時得爲別部司馬，后常對太祖怨言，太祖荅言：「但得與我作婦弟，不爲多邪？」

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: At first, Empress Bian's younger brother Bing, during the Jian'an era, was able to become a Separate Commandment Major; the empress often voiced grievances to the Grand Progenitor about him, and the Grand Progenitor replied, saying, "Is it not already much that he gets to be my brother-in-law?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that at first, during Jian'an, Empress Bian's younger brother Bing became a Major of a Separate Unit. The empress often complained about him to the Grand Progenitor, who answered, "Is it not already much that he gets to be my brother-in-law?"

sentences.zh: 后又欲太祖給其錢帛，太祖又曰：「但汝盜與，不爲足邪？」

translations.literal: Later the empress also wanted the Grand Progenitor to supply him with money and silks; the Grand Progenitor again said, "Is it not enough that you secretly give to him?"
translations.idiomatic: Later she also wanted the Grand Progenitor to supply him with money and silks. He replied again, "Is it not enough that you secretly give to him?"

sentences.zh: 故訖太祖世，秉官不移，財亦不益。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout the Grand Progenitor's lifetime Bing's office did not change and his wealth was not increased.
translations.idiomatic: So throughout the Grand Progenitor's lifetime Bing's office never changed and his wealth was never increased.

sentences.zh: 秉薨，子蘭嗣。

translations.literal: When Bing died, his son Lan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing died, his son Lan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 少有才學，《魏略》曰：蘭獻賦贊述太子德美，太子報曰：「賦者，言事類之所附也，頌者，美盛德之形容也，故作者不虛其辭，受者必當其實。

translations.literal: He had talent and learning from youth. The Wei Summary states: Lan presented fu and praise describing the heir apparent's virtuous beauty; the heir apparent replied, saying, "The fu states the categories to which affairs attach; the song praises the appearance of flourishing virtue. Therefore the author must not empty his words, and the recipient must match the reality.
translations.idiomatic: He showed talent and learning from youth. The Wei Summary says Lan presented fu and praise describing the heir apparent's virtues. The heir apparent replied, "The fu states the categories to which affairs attach; the song praises the form of flourishing virtue. The author must not empty his words, and the recipient must match the reality.

sentences.zh: 蘭此賦，豈吾實哉？

translations.literal: Is this fu of Lan truly my reality?
translations.idiomatic: Is this fu of Lan truly my reality?

sentences.zh: 昔吾丘壽王一陳寶鼎，何武等徒以歌頌，猶受金帛之賜，蘭事雖不諒，義足嘉也。

translations.literal: In former times when Liu Qiu, King Shou of Wu, once presented the precious tripod, He Wu and the rest merely sang in praise yet still received gifts of gold and silks. Lan's matter, though not to be credited, is worthy enough to commend.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qiu, King Shou of Wu, once presented the precious tripod, He Wu and others merely sang in praise yet still received gold and silks. Lan's matter, though not to be credited, is still worthy of commendation.

sentences.zh: 今賜牛一頭。」

translations.literal: Now I grant one ox."
translations.idiomatic: Now I grant one ox."

sentences.zh: 由是遂見親敬。

translations.literal: From this he came to be treated with intimacy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: From this he came to be treated with intimacy and respect.

sentences.zh: 爲奉車都尉、游擊將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He served as Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and General Who Attacks Independently, with the additional post of Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commandant of the imperial carriage and general who attacks independently, with the additional post of regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 蘭薨，子暉嗣。

translations.literal: When Lan died, his son Hui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan died, his son Hui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：明帝時，蘭見外有二難，而帝留意於宮室，常因侍從，數切諫。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: During Ming-di's reign Lan saw that externally there were two difficulties while the emperor focused on palace construction; he often took occasion while attending in close service to remonstrate sharply and repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that during Emperor Ming's reign, Lan saw two external crises while the emperor focused his attention on palace buildings. He often used occasions of attendance and service to remonstrate sharply and repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不能從，猶納其誠欵。

translations.literal: Although the emperor could not follow his advice, he still accepted his sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor could not follow his advice, he still accepted his sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 後蘭苦酒消渴，時帝信巫女用水方，使人持水賜蘭，蘭不肯飲。

translations.literal: Later Lan suffered from wine-induced thirst; at the time the emperor trusted a shamaness's water prescription and sent someone bearing water to grant to Lan, but Lan refused to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lan suffered from wine-induced thirst. The emperor trusted a shamaness's water prescription and sent water for him, but Lan refused to drink.

sentences.zh: 詔問其意？

translations.literal: An edict asked his meaning?
translations.idiomatic: An edict asked why.

sentences.zh: 蘭言治病自當以方藥，何信於此？

translations.literal: Lan said that treating illness should naturally rely on prescriptions and medicines—why trust in this?
translations.idiomatic: Lan said illness should be treated with prescriptions and medicines—why trust in this?

sentences.zh: 帝爲變色，而蘭終不服。

translations.literal: The emperor changed countenance, yet Lan to the end did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed countenance, yet Lan to the end would not submit.

sentences.zh: 後渴稍甚，以至於亡。

translations.literal: Later his thirst grew somewhat worse, until it led to his death.
translations.idiomatic: Later his thirst grew worse until he died.

sentences.zh: 故時人見蘭好直言，謂帝靣折之而蘭自殺，其實不然。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time, seeing Lan's love of blunt speech, said the emperor had shamed him to his face and Lan killed himself—but in fact it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time, seeing Lan's love of blunt speech, said the emperor had shamed him to his face and Lan killed himself—but in fact it was not so.

sentences.zh: 又分秉爵，封蘭弟琳爲列侯，官至步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Bing's noble rank was also divided, and Lan's younger brother Lin was enfeoffed as a full marquis, reaching the office of Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's noble rank was also divided, and Lan's younger brother Lin was enfeoffed as a full marquis and reached the office of colonel of the footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 蘭子隆女爲高貴鄉公皇后，隆以后父爲光祿大夫，位特進，封睢陽鄉侯，妻王爲顯陽鄉君。

translations.literal: Lan's son Long had a daughter who became empress to the Duke of Gaoguixiang; Long, as the empress's father, was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the position of Special Advance, enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiyang Village, and his wife Wang was made Lady of Xianyang Village.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's son Long had a daughter who became empress to the Duke of Gaoguixiang. Long, as the empress's father, was made grand master for splendid happiness with the rank of special advance, enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiyang village, and his wife Wang was made lady of Xianyang village.

sentences.zh: 追封隆前妻劉爲順陽鄉君，后親母故也。

translations.literal: Long's former wife Liu was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Shunyang Village, because she was the empress's birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: Long's former wife Liu was posthumously enfeoffed as lady of Shunyang village, because she was the empress's birth mother.

sentences.zh: 琳女又爲陳留王皇后，時琳已沒，封琳妻劉爲廣陽鄉君。

translations.literal: Lin's daughter also became empress to the Prince of Chenliu; Lin was already dead, so Lin's wife Liu was enfeoffed as Lady of Guangyang Village.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's daughter also became empress to the Prince of Chenliu. Lin was already dead, so his wife Liu was enfeoffed as lady of Guangyang village.

sentences.zh: 文昭甄皇后，中山無極人，明帝母，漢太保甄邯後也，世吏二千石。

translations.literal: Empress Wen-Zhao, née Zhen, was a native of Wuji in Zhongshan, mother of Ming-di, a descendant of Han's Grand Tutor Zhen Han; for generations her family held offices of two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen-Zhao of the Zhen clan came from Wuji in Zhongshan. She was Ming-di's mother and a descendant of Han's grand tutor Zhen Han; for generations her family held offices of two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 父逸，上蔡令。

translations.literal: Her father Yi was Magistrate of Shangcai.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yi was magistrate of Shangcai.

sentences.zh: 后三歲失父。

translations.literal: The empress lost her father at age three.
translations.idiomatic: The empress lost her father at age three.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：逸娶常山張氏，生三男五女：長男豫，早終；

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Yi married a woman of the Zhang clan of Changshan and had three sons and five daughters: the eldest son Yu died early;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Yi married a woman of the Zhang clan of Changshan and had three sons and five daughters: the eldest son Yu died early;

sentences.zh: 次儼，舉孝廉，大將軍掾、曲梁長；

translations.literal: the second, Yan, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, served as aide to the Grand General, and was Magistrate of Quliang;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Yan, was recommended as filial and incorrupt, served as aide to the grand general, and was magistrate of Quliang;

sentences.zh: 次堯，舉孝廉；

translations.literal: the third, Yao, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt;
translations.idiomatic: the third, Yao, was recommended as filial and incorrupt;

sentences.zh: 長女姜，次脫，次道，次榮，次即后。

translations.literal: the eldest daughter Jiang, then Tuo, then Dao, then Rong, and last was the empress.
translations.idiomatic: the eldest daughter Jiang, then Tuo, then Dao, then Rong, and last the empress.

sentences.zh: 后以漢光和五年十二月丁酉生。

translations.literal: The empress was born on the dingyou day of the twelfth month of the fifth year of Guanghe of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was born on dingyou in the twelfth month of Han Guanghe 5.

sentences.zh: 每寢寐，家中彷彿見如有人持玉衣覆其上者，常共怪之。

translations.literal: Whenever she slept, the household seemed to see as if someone held a jade garment covering her; they constantly marveled at it together.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she slept, the household seemed to see someone holding a jade garment over her, and they all marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 逸薨，加號慕，內外益奇之。

translations.literal: When Yi died, her grief was called deep and yearning; inside and outside the family all the more found her extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died, her deep mourning made everyone inside and outside the family find her all the more extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 後相者劉良相后及諸子，良指后曰：「此女貴乃不可言。」

translations.literal: Later the physiognomist Liu Liang read the empress and all the children; Liang pointed to the empress and said, "This girl's nobility is beyond words."
translations.idiomatic: Later the physiognomist Liu Liang read the empress and all the children. Pointing to her he said, "This girl's nobility is beyond words."

sentences.zh: 后自少至長，不好戲弄。

translations.literal: From youth to adulthood the empress did not care for playful amusement.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to adulthood the empress cared nothing for playful amusement.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，外有立騎馬戲者，家人諸姊皆上閣觀之，后獨不行。

translations.literal: At age eight, outside there were performers standing on horseback; all the sisters in the family went up to the gallery to watch, but the empress alone would not go.
translations.idiomatic: At age eight, when mounted performers put on a show outside, all her sisters went up to the gallery to watch, but the empress alone would not go.

sentences.zh: 諸姊怪問之，后答言：「此豈女人之所觀邪？」

translations.literal: Her sisters wondered and asked her; the empress answered, saying, "Is this something a woman should watch?"
translations.idiomatic: Her sisters wondered and asked her. She answered, "Is this something a woman should watch?"

sentences.zh: 年九歲，喜書，視字輒識，數用諸兄筆硯，兄謂后言：「汝當習女工。

translations.literal: At age nine she loved books; seeing characters she immediately knew them, and often used her elder brothers' brush and inkstone. An elder brother said to the empress, "You should practice women's work.
translations.idiomatic: At age nine she loved books; seeing characters she immediately knew them, and often used her elder brothers' brush and inkstone. An elder brother told her, "You should practice women's work.

sentences.zh: 用書為學，當作女博士邪？」

translations.literal: To take books as learning—are you to become a female scholar?"
translations.idiomatic: To take books as learning—are you to become a female scholar?"

sentences.zh: 后答言：「聞古者賢女，未有不學前世成敗，以為己誡。

translations.literal: The empress answered, saying, "I have heard that in antiquity worthy women all studied the successes and failures of former ages and took them as warnings for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "I have heard that in antiquity worthy women all studied the successes and failures of former ages and took them as warnings for themselves.

sentences.zh: 不知書，何由見之？」

translations.literal: Without knowing books, how could one see them?"
translations.idiomatic: Without knowing books, how could one see them?"

sentences.zh: 後天下兵亂，加以饑饉，百姓皆賣金銀珠玉寶物，時后家大有儲谷，頗以買之。

translations.literal: Later the realm fell into military disorder, and famine was added; common people all sold gold, silver, pearls, jade, and precious goods. At the time the empress's family had great stores of grain and bought such things in considerable quantity.
translations.idiomatic: Later the realm fell into war and famine, and common people sold gold, silver, pearls, jade, and precious goods. The empress's family had great stores of grain and bought such things in considerable quantity.

sentences.zh: 后年十餘歲，白母曰：「今世亂而多買寶物，匹夫無罪，懷璧為罪。

translations.literal: When the empress was just over ten she told her mother, saying, "In this age of disorder, to buy many precious goods—an ordinary man without guilt becomes guilty for holding a jade disc.
translations.idiomatic: When she was just over ten she told her mother, "In this age of disorder, to buy many precious goods—an ordinary man without guilt becomes guilty for holding a jade disc.

sentences.zh: 又左右皆飢乏，不如以穀振給親族鄰里，廣為恩惠也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, those around us are all hungry and in want—it would be better to use grain to relieve and supply kin and neighbors and spread kindness broadly."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those around us are all hungry and in want. It would be better to use grain to relieve kin and neighbors and spread kindness broadly."

sentences.zh: 舉家稱善，即從后言。

translations.literal: The whole family praised this as good and immediately followed the empress's words.
translations.idiomatic: The whole family praised this as good and immediately followed her advice.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：后年十四，喪中兄儼，悲哀過制，事寡嫂謙敬，事處其勞，拊養儼子，慈愛甚篤。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: At age fourteen the empress mourned her elder brother Yan; her grief exceeded the prescribed measure. She served her widowed sister-in-law with modest reverence, took on the labor in affairs, and nurtured Yan's son with deep loving care.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that at age fourteen she mourned her elder brother Yan with grief beyond the prescribed measure. She served her widowed sister-in-law with modest reverence, took on the labor herself, and nurtured Yan's son with deep loving care.

sentences.zh: 后母性嚴，待諸婦有常，后數諫母：「兄不幸早終，嫂年少守節，顧留一子，以大義言之，待之當如婦，愛之宜如女。」

translations.literal: The empress's mother was strict by nature and treated the various daughters-in-law with fixed rules. The empress repeatedly admonished her mother: "Elder brother unhappily died early; sister-in-law is young and keeps chastity, yet she has left one son. Speaking by great principle, she should be treated as a daughter-in-law and loved as a daughter."
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother was strict by nature and treated the daughters-in-law by fixed rules. The empress repeatedly admonished her: "Elder brother died early; sister-in-law is young and keeps chastity, yet she has left one son. By great principle she should be treated as a daughter-in-law and loved as a daughter."

sentences.zh: 母感后言流涕，便令后與嫂共止，寢息坐起常相隨，恩愛益密。

translations.literal: The mother was moved by the empress's words to weeping and immediately had the empress and sister-in-law lodge together; in sleeping, rising, sitting, and moving they constantly kept each other company, and their affection grew ever closer.
translations.idiomatic: The mother was moved to tears and had the empress lodge with her sister-in-law. In sleeping, rising, sitting, and moving they constantly kept each other company, and their affection grew ever closer.

sentences.zh: 建安中，袁紹為中子熙納之。

translations.literal: During Jian'an, Yuan Shao had his middle son Xi take her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: During Jian'an, Yuan Shao had his middle son Xi take her in marriage.

sentences.zh: 熙出為幽州，后留養姑。

translations.literal: Xi went out to You Province, and the empress remained to nurture her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Xi went out to You Province, and she remained to care for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 及冀州平，文帝納后於鄴，有寵，生明帝及東鄉公主。

translations.literal: When Ji Province was pacified, Wen-di took the empress in marriage at Ye; she had favor and bore Ming-di and the Princess of Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Province was pacified, Wen-di took her in marriage at Ye. She won favor and bore Ming-di and the Princess of Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：熙出在幽州，后留侍姑。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: Xi went out to You Province, and the empress remained to attend her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that Xi went out to Youzhou, and the empress remained to attend her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 及鄴城破，紹妻及后共坐皇堂上。

translations.literal: When Ye city fell, Yuan Shao's wife and the empress sat together in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye fell, Yuan Shao's wife and the empress sat together in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 文帝入紹舍，見紹妻及后，后怖，以頭伏姑膝上，紹妻兩手自搏。

translations.literal: Wen-di entered Yuan Shao's residence and saw Yuan Shao's wife and the empress; the empress was afraid and laid her head on her mother-in-law's knee, while Yuan Shao's wife beat her own hands together.
translations.idiomatic: Wen-di entered Yuan Shao's residence and saw Yuan Shao's wife and the empress. She was afraid and laid her head on her mother-in-law's knee, while Yuan Shao's wife beat her own hands together.

sentences.zh: 文帝謂曰：「劉夫人云何如此？

translations.literal: Wen-di said, "Lady Liu, why are you like this?
translations.idiomatic: Wen-di said, "Lady Liu, why are you like this?

sentences.zh: 令新婦舉頭！」

translations.literal: Have the new bride lift her head!"
translations.idiomatic: Have the new bride lift her head!"

sentences.zh: 姑乃捧后令仰，文帝就視，見其顏色非凡，稱嘆之。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law then lifted the empress and made her raise her face; Wen-di drew near to look and saw her countenance was extraordinary, and praised her in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law lifted her and made her raise her face. Emperor Wen drew near to look, saw that her countenance was extraordinary, and praised her in admiration.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其意，遂為迎取。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard of his intent and thereupon had her welcomed and taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor heard of his intent and had her welcomed and taken.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：太祖下鄴，文帝先入袁尚府，有婦人被髮垢面，垂涕立紹妻劉後，文帝問之，劉答「是熙妻」，顧攬髮髻，以巾拭面，姿貌絕倫。

translations.literal: Accounts of the Age states: When the Grand Progenitor descended on Ye, Wen-di first entered Yuan Shang's mansion. A woman with hair loose and face filthy stood weeping behind Yuan Shao's wife Liu. Wen-di asked about her; Liu answered, "She is Xi's wife." She turned, gathered her hair into a bun, wiped her face with a kerchief, and her bearing and beauty were unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts of the Age says that when the Grand Progenitor descended on Ye, Wen-di first entered Yuan Shang's mansion. A woman with hair loose and face filthy stood weeping behind Yuan Shao's wife Liu. Wen-di asked about her; Liu answered, "She is Xi's wife." She turned, gathered her hair into a bun, wiped her face with a kerchief, and her bearing and beauty were unmatched.

sentences.zh: 既過，劉謂后「不憂死矣」！

translations.literal: After he had passed, Liu said to the empress, "You need not fear death now!"
translations.idiomatic: After he had passed, Liu told her, "You need not fear death now!"

sentences.zh: 遂見納，有寵。

translations.literal: She was then taken in marriage and had favor.
translations.idiomatic: She was then taken in marriage and won favor.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：后寵愈隆而彌自挹損，後宮有寵者勸勉之，其無寵者慰誨之，每因閒宴，常勸帝，言「昔黃帝子孫蕃育，蓋由妾媵眾多，乃獲斯祚耳。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: As the empress's favor grew ever greater she all the more restrained herself. To favored women of the inner palace she offered encouragement; to those without favor she gave comfort and instruction. At every idle banquet she often urged the emperor, saying, "In former times the Yellow Emperor's descendants multiplied and flourished—likely because concubines and secondary wives were many, and thereby this blessing was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says that as her favor grew ever greater she all the more restrained herself. To favored women of the inner palace she offered encouragement; to those without favor she gave comfort and instruction. At every idle banquet she often urged the emperor, saying, "In former times the Yellow Emperor's descendants multiplied and flourished—likely because concubines and secondary wives were many, and thereby this blessing was obtained.

sentences.zh: 所原廣求淑媛，以豐繼嗣。」

translations.literal: What I desire is broadly to seek worthy maidens to enrich the succession."
translations.idiomatic: What I desire is broadly to seek worthy maidens to enrich the succession."

sentences.zh: 帝心嘉焉。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's heart approved this.

sentences.zh: 其後帝欲遣任氏，后請於帝曰：「任既鄉黨名族，德、色，妾等不及也，如何遣之？」

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor wished to send away Lady Ren. The empress pleaded with the emperor, saying, "Ren is a famous clan of our native district; in virtue and beauty your handmaids do not match her—how can you send her away?"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor wished to send away Lady Ren. The empress pleaded with him, saying, "Ren is a famous clan of our native district; in virtue and beauty we do not match her—how can you send her away?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「任性狷急不婉順，前後忿吾非一，是以遣之耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Ren's nature is narrow and urgent, not gentle and compliant; before and after she has been angry with me more than once—therefore I send her away."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Lady Ren is narrow and quick-tempered, not gentle or compliant. She has been angry with me more than once, and that is why I am sending her away."

sentences.zh: 后流涕固請曰：「妾受敬遇之恩，眾人所知，必謂任之出，是妾之由。

translations.literal: The empress wept and firmly pleaded, saying, "Your handmaid has received the grace of respectful treatment—this all know. They will surely say Ren's dismissal is because of your handmaid.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept and firmly pleaded, saying, "Your handmaid has received the grace of respectful treatment—this all know. They will surely say Ren's dismissal is because of me.

sentences.zh: 上懼有見私之譏，下受專寵之罪，原重留意！」

translations.literal: Above I fear the reproach of showing partiality; below I would bear the guilt of monopolizing favor—I beg you to reconsider carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: Above I fear the reproach of showing partiality; below I would bear the guilt of monopolizing favor—I beg you to reconsider carefully!"

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，遂出之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen and thereupon sent her out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen and sent her out.

sentences.zh: 十六年七月，太祖徵關中，武宣皇后從，留孟津，帝居守鄴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixteenth year the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Guanzhong; Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan followed, remaining at Mengjin, while the emperor stayed to guard Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year sixteen the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Guanzhong. Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan followed and remained at Mengjin, while Wen-di stayed to guard Ye.

sentences.zh: 時武宣皇后體小不安，后不得定省，憂怖，晝夜泣涕；

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan's body was slightly unwell; the empress could not attend to inquire after her and was anxious and fearful, weeping day and night;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan was slightly unwell. The empress could not attend to inquire after her and was anxious and fearful, weeping day and night;

sentences.zh: 左右驟以差問告，后猶不信，曰：「夫人在家，故疾每動，輒歷時，今疾便差，何速也？

translations.literal: attendants suddenly reported that she had improved; the empress still did not believe and said, "When the lady was at home, whenever her old illness stirred it always lasted some time. Now the illness has suddenly improved—how can it be so quick?
translations.idiomatic: attendants suddenly reported that she had improved. The empress still did not believe and said, "When the lady was at home, whenever her old illness stirred it always lasted some time. Now the illness has suddenly improved—how can it be so quick?

sentences.zh: 此欲慰我意耳！」

translations.literal: This is only to comfort my feelings!"
translations.idiomatic: This is only to comfort my feelings!"

sentences.zh: 憂愈甚。

translations.literal: Her worry grew all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: Her worry grew all the greater.

sentences.zh: 后得武宣皇后還書，說疾已平復，后乃懽悅。

translations.literal: When the empress received Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan's reply saying the illness had already fully recovered, she then rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When she received Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan's reply saying the illness had fully recovered, she rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，大軍還鄴，后朝武宣皇后，望幄座悲喜，感動左右。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year the great army returned to Ye; the empress attended upon Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, and gazing at the curtained seat felt both grief and joy, moving those around her.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year seventeen the great army returned to Ye. The empress attended upon Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, and gazing at the curtained seat felt both grief and joy, moving those around her.

sentences.zh: 武宣皇后見后如此，亦泣，且謂之曰：「新婦謂吾前病如昔時困邪？

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, seeing the empress like this, also wept and said to her, "Does the new bride think my former illness was like the distress of former times?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, seeing her like this, also wept and said, "Does the new bride think my former illness was like the distress of former times?

sentences.zh: 吾時小小耳，十餘日即差，不當視我顏色乎！」

translations.literal: At the time it was only slight; in little more than ten days it was cured—you should not have looked at my complexion so!"
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was only slight; in little more than ten days it was cured—you should not have looked at my complexion so!"

sentences.zh: 嗟歎曰：「此真孝婦也。」

translations.literal: She sighed in admiration and said, "This is truly a filial daughter-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: She sighed in admiration and said, "This is truly a filial daughter-in-law."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，太祖東征，武宣皇后、文帝及明帝、東鄉公主皆從，時后以病留鄴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Grand Progenitor campaigned east; Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, Wen-di, Ming-di, and the Princess of Dongxiang all followed, while at the time the empress remained at Ye because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one the Grand Progenitor campaigned east. Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, Wen-di, Ming-di, and the Princess of Dongxiang all followed, while the empress remained at Ye because of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十二年九月，大軍還，武宣皇后左右侍御見后顏色豐盈，怪問之曰：「后與二子別久，下流之情，不可為念，而后顏色更盛，何也？」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year the great army returned; attendants around Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan saw the empress's complexion full and flourishing, wondered, and asked, saying, "The empress has been apart from her two sons for long; the feelings of parting should not be forgotten, yet her complexion is even more radiant—why?"
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year twenty-two the great army returned. Attendants around Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan saw the empress's complexion full and flourishing, wondered, and asked, "The empress has been apart from her two sons for long; the feelings of parting should not be forgotten, yet her complexion is even more radiant—why?"

sentences.zh: 后笑答之曰：「

translations.literal: The empress laughed and answered: "
translations.idiomatic: The empress laughed and answered: "

translations.idiomatic: (tabooed)

translations.literal: and the rest follow the lady by themselves—what should I worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: and the rest follow the lady by themselves—what should I worry about!"

sentences.zh: 后之賢明以禮自持如此。

translations.literal: The empress's wisdom and clarity, holding herself by ritual, were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the empress's wisdom and restraint in holding herself by ritual.

sentences.zh: 延康元年220年正月，文帝即王位，六月，南征，后留鄴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yankang (220 CE) Wen-di took the royal title; in the sixth month he campaigned south, and the empress remained at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yankang 1 (220 CE) Wen-di took the royal title. In the sixth month he campaigned south, and the empress remained at Ye.

sentences.zh: 黃初元年十月，帝踐阼。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Huangchu the emperor ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Huangchu 1 the emperor ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 踐阼之後，山陽公奉二女以嬪於魏，郭后、李、陰貴人並愛幸，后愈失意，有怨言。

translations.literal: After ascending the throne, the Duke of Shanyang presented two daughters to become consorts of Wei; Empress Guo and the Honored Ladies Li and Yin were all favored and cherished; the empress grew ever more disappointed and had resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: After ascending the throne, the Duke of Shanyang presented two daughters to become consorts of Wei. Empress Guo and the Honored Ladies Li and Yin were all favored, and the empress grew ever more disappointed and spoke resentfully.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，二年六月，遣使賜死，葬於鄴。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; in the sixth month of the second year he sent an envoy to grant death, and she was buried at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered. In the sixth month of year two he sent an envoy to grant death, and she was buried at Ye.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：有司奏建長秋宮，帝璽書迎后，詣行在所，后上表曰：「妾聞先代之興，所以饗國久長，垂祚後嗣，無不由后妃焉。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: The responsible officials memorialized to establish the Palace of Everlasting Autumn; the emperor sent an imperial patent to welcome the empress to the traveling residence. The empress submitted a memorial, saying, "Your handmaid has heard that the rise of former ages, whereby states were nourished long and blessings were handed down to later heirs, was never without empresses and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says officials memorialized to establish the Palace of Everlasting Autumn, and the emperor sent an imperial patent to welcome the empress to the traveling residence. She submitted a memorial, saying, "Your handmaid has heard that the rise of former ages, whereby states were nourished long and blessings were handed down to later heirs, was never without empresses and consorts.

sentences.zh: 故必審選其人，以興內教。

translations.literal: Therefore one must carefully select the person to raise inner instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one must carefully select the person to raise inner instruction.

sentences.zh: 令踐阼之初，誠宜登進賢淑，統理六宮。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of ascending the throne it is truly fitting to advance the worthy and virtuous to govern the six palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Now at the beginning of ascending the throne it is truly fitting to advance the worthy and virtuous to govern the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 妾自省愚陋，不任粢盛之事，加以寢疾，敢守微志。」

translations.literal: Your handmaid examines herself as foolish and base, unfit for the charge of sacrificial grain, and moreover afflicted with lingering illness—I dare hold to my modest wish."
translations.idiomatic: Your handmaid knows herself to be foolish and lowly, unfit to take charge of the sacrificial grain; moreover I am confined by lingering illness, and so I dare hold to my humble wish."

sentences.zh: 璽書三至而后三讓，言甚懇切。

translations.literal: Imperial patents came three times and the empress yielded three times; her words were very earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial patents came three times and she yielded three times; her words were very earnest and sincere.

sentences.zh: 時盛暑，帝欲須秋涼乃更迎后。

translations.literal: It was then the height of summer; the emperor wished to wait until autumn's cool before welcoming the empress again.
translations.idiomatic: It was then the height of summer; the emperor wished to wait until autumn's cool before welcoming her again.

sentences.zh: 會后疾遂篤，夏六月丁卯，崩於鄴。

translations.literal: But the empress's illness then grew grave; on dingmao in the sixth month of summer she died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: But her illness then grew grave. On dingmao in the sixth month of summer she died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 帝哀痛咨嗟，策贈皇后璽綬。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned in grief and lamentation and by patent granted the empress's seal and sash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned in grief and lamentation and by patent granted the empress's seal and sash.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以為春秋之義，內大惡諱，小惡不書。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that by the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, great evils within are tabooed and not written, while small evils are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi considers that by the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, great evils within are tabooed and not written, while small evils are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 文帝之不立甄氏，及加殺害，事有明審。

translations.literal: Wen-di's not establishing the Zhen clan, and moreover adding execution—the matter is clearly established.
translations.idiomatic: Wen-di's not establishing Lady Zhen, and moreover putting her to death—the matter is clearly established.

sentences.zh: 魏史若以為大惡邪，則宜隱而不言，若謂為小惡邪，則不應假為之辭，而崇飾虛文乃至於是，異乎所聞於舊史。

translations.literal: If the Wei historians considered it a great evil, then they should have concealed it and not spoken; if they called it a small evil, then they should not have fabricated words for it and exalted and adorned empty prose to this extent—this differs from what one hears in the old histories.
translations.idiomatic: If the Wei historians considered it a great evil, they should have concealed it and not spoken; if they called it a small evil, they should not have fabricated words and exalted empty prose to this extent—this differs from what one hears in the old histories.

sentences.zh: 推此而言，其稱卞、甄諸后言行之善，皆難以實論。

translations.literal: Extending this to speak, their praise of the good conduct and words of Empresses Bian, Zhen, and the rest—all are hard to judge by reality.
translations.idiomatic: Extending this to speak, their praise of the good conduct and words of Empresses Bian, Zhen, and the rest are all hard to judge by reality.

sentences.zh: 陳氏刪落，良有以也。

translations.literal: Chen Shou's deletions were well founded.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou's deletions were well founded.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，有司奏請追諡，使司空王朗持節奉策以太牢告祠於陵，又別立寢廟。

translations.literal: When Ming-di succeeded to the throne, the responsible officials memorialized requesting a posthumous title; they sent Minister of Works Wang Lang, bearing the staff of office, to present the edict with the grand sacrifice and announce the rite at the tomb, and also to establish a separate private temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne, the responsible officials memorialized requesting a posthumous title. They sent Wang Lang, Minister of Works, bearing the staff, to present the patent and announce the rite at the tomb with a grand sacrifice, and they also established a separate sleeping temple.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》載三公奏曰：「蓋孝敬之道，篤乎其親，乃四海所以承化，天地所以明察，是謂生則致其養，歿則光其靈，誦述以盡其美，宣揚以顯其名者也。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei records that the Three Dukes submitted: "Filial reverence and respect for parents lie deep in devotion to one's kin; thereby the four seas receive transformation and heaven and earth gain clear discernment. This means that while living one renders full nurture, and after death one glorifies the spirit; recitation and narration exhaust their beauty, and proclamation and display make their names manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records the Three Dukes' memorial: "Filial reverence begins in deep devotion to one's kin. Through it the four seas receive moral instruction and heaven and earth gain clear sight. While the living owe full nurture, the dead deserve that their spirits be honored; their virtues should be recounted to the full and their names proclaimed abroad.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以聖懿之德，紹承洪業，至孝烝烝，通於神明，遭罹殷憂，每勞謙讓。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, with sagely and virtuous conduct, has succeeded to the great enterprise; your utmost filial piety is abundant and reaches the spirits; having suffered deep grief, you repeatedly labor in modest yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, with sagely virtue, has inherited the great enterprise. Your filial devotion reaches the spirits, and in deep grief you have repeatedly insisted on modest restraint.

sentences.zh: 先帝遷神山陵，大禮既備，至於先后，未有顯諡。

translations.literal: The late emperor was moved to the spirit mountain tomb and the great rites were complete, yet as for the former empress, no illustrious posthumous title had been granted.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor had been laid in the imperial tomb and the great rites were complete, yet the former empress still lacked an illustrious posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 伏惟先后恭讓著於幽微，至行顯於不言，化流邦國，德侔二南，故能膺神靈嘉祥，為大魏世妃。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that the former empress's modest yielding was manifest in hidden places and her utmost conduct shone in what was left unsaid; her transforming influence flowed through the realm and her virtue matched the Two Nan odes; therefore she received the spirits' auspicious blessing and became Great Wei's consort for the ages.
translations.idiomatic: The former empress showed modest yielding in the smallest matters and supreme conduct in deeds rather than words. Her influence flowed through the realm and her virtue matched the Two Nan odes, so she received heaven's blessing and became Great Wei's consort for the ages.

sentences.zh: 雖夙年登遐，萬載之後，永播融烈，后妃之功莫得而尚也。

translations.literal: Although she early departed this life, after ten thousand ages her radiant glory will forever be spread abroad; the achievement of empresses and consorts cannot be surpassed.
translations.idiomatic: Though she died young, her radiant merit will shine for ages to come; no empress or consort could surpass her.

sentences.zh: 案諡法：『聖聞周達曰昭。

translations.literal: Examining the posthumous-title canon: 'One whose sagely repute is thorough and far-reaching is called Zhao.'
translations.idiomatic: The canon of posthumous titles says, "One whose sagely repute is thorough and far-reaching is called Zhao."

sentences.zh: 德明有功曰昭。』

translations.literal: One whose virtue is bright and whose merit is established is called Zhao.'
translations.idiomatic: One whose virtue is bright and whose merit is established is called Zhao."

sentences.zh: 昭者，光明之至，盛久而不昧者也。

translations.literal: Zhao means the utmost of brightness, flourishing long without dimming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao means the utmost brightness, flourishing long without fading.

sentences.zh: 宜上尊諡曰文昭皇后。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to raise the honored posthumous title Wen-Zhao Empress."
translations.idiomatic: We should grant the posthumous title Empress Wen-Zhao."

sentences.zh: 是月，三公又奏曰：「自古週人始祖后稷，又特立廟以祀姜嫄。

translations.literal: That month the Three Dukes again submitted: "From antiquity the Zhou people's founding ancestor Hou Ji also had a separate temple established to sacrifice to Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Three Dukes memorialized again: "From antiquity the Zhou people's founding ancestor Hou Ji also had a separate temple set up to honor Jiang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 今文昭皇后之於萬嗣，聖德至化，豈有量哉！

translations.literal: Now Empress Wen-Zhao's sagely virtue and utmost transforming power toward myriad heirs—how could they be measured!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen-Zhao's sagely virtue and transforming power toward all posterity—how could they be measured!

translations.literal: Examining ancient institutions, it is fitting to follow the Rites of Zhou and establish a separate private temple for the founding mother."
translations.idiomatic: By ancient precedent and the Rites of Zhou, a separate private temple should be established for the founding mother."
