translations.literal: Both memorials were submitted and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials were approved.

sentences.zh: 太和元年227年三月，以中山魏昌之安城鄉戶千，追封逸，諡曰敬侯；

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Taihe (227 CE), with the thousand households of Ancheng Township in Weichang, Zhongshan, Yi was posthumously enfeoffed and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Taihe 1 (227 CE), Yi was posthumously enfeoffed with the thousand households of Ancheng Township in Weichang, Zhongshan, and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing;

sentences.zh: 適孫像襲爵。

translations.literal: his eldest grandson Xiang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: his eldest grandson Xiang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 四月，初營宗廟，掘地得玉璽，方一寸九分，其文曰「天子羨思慈親」，明帝為之改容，以太牢告廟。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, when the ancestral temple was first being built, a jade seal was dug from the ground, one inch and nine tenths square; its inscription read "The Son of Heaven admires and thinks of his gracious parent." Ming-di changed countenance at this and announced it to the temple with the grand sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, while the ancestral temple was first being built, workers unearthed a jade seal one inch and nine tenths square inscribed "The Son of Heaven admires and thinks of his gracious parent." Ming-di changed countenance and announced it to the temple with the grand sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又嘗夢見后，於是差次舅氏親疏高下，敘用各有差，賞賜累鉅萬；

translations.literal: He also once dreamed of the empress; thereupon he ranked his maternal kin by closeness and distance, high and low, appointing and employing each with distinctions, and bestowed rewards totaling tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: He also once dreamed of the empress. Thereupon he ranked his maternal kin by closeness and distance, appointing each according to rank and bestowing rewards totaling tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 以像為虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Xiang was made Colonel of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was made Colonel of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 是月，后母薨，帝制緦服臨喪，百僚陪位。

translations.literal: That month the empress's mother died; the emperor wore the coarsest mourning and attended the funeral, and the hundred officials took their places in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: That month the empress's mother died. The emperor wore the coarsest mourning and attended the funeral, with the hundred officials in attendance.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，以后舊陵庳下，使像兼太尉，持節詣鄴，昭告后土，十二月，改葬朝陽陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, because the empress's old tomb was low and small, Xiang was made Acting Grand Commandant and sent with the staff of office to Ye to announce the rite to Queen Earth; in the twelfth month she was reburied at Chaoyang Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year four, because the empress's old tomb was too low and small, Xiang was made Acting Grand Commandant and sent with the imperial staff to Ye to announce the rite to Queen Earth. In the twelfth month she was reburied at Chaoyang Tomb.

sentences.zh: 像還，遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Xiang returned, he was transferred to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang returned, he was transferred to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年春，追諡后兄儼曰安城鄉穆侯。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Qinglong, the empress's elder brother Yan was posthumously titled Marquis Mu of Ancheng Township.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qinglong 2, the empress's elder brother Yan was posthumously titled Marquis Mu of Ancheng Township.

sentences.zh: 夏，吳賊寇揚州，以像為伏波將軍，持節監諸將東征，還，復為射聲校尉。

translations.literal: In summer Wu bandits raided Yang Province; Xiang was made General Who Calms the Waves and, bearing the staff of office, supervised the generals in the eastern campaign; on his return he again became Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.
translations.idiomatic: In summer Wu raiders attacked Yangzhou. Xiang was made General Who Calms the Waves and, bearing the staff, supervised the generals in the eastern campaign. On his return he again became Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.

sentences.zh: 三年薨，追贈衛將軍，改封魏昌縣，諡曰貞侯；

translations.literal: In the third year he died; posthumously he was granted General of the Guard, his fief was changed to Weichang County, and he was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died. He was posthumously made General of the Guard, his fief was changed to Weichang County, and he received the posthumous title Marquis Zhen;

sentences.zh: 子暢嗣。

translations.literal: his son Chang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: his son Chang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 又封暢弟溫、韡、艷皆為列侯。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brothers Wen, Wei, and Yan were also all enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brothers Wen, Wei, and Yan were also all enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 四年，改逸、儼本封皆曰魏昌侯，諡因故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the original fiefs of Yi and Yan were both changed to Marquis of Weichang, their posthumous titles remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the original fiefs of Yi and Yan were both changed to Marquis of Weichang, their posthumous titles remaining unchanged.

sentences.zh: 封儼世婦劉為東鄉君，又追封逸世婦張為安喜君。

translations.literal: Yan's daughter-in-law Liu was enfeoffed as Lady of Dongxiang, and Yi's daughter-in-law Zhang was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's daughter-in-law Liu was enfeoffed as Lady of Dongxiang, and Yi's daughter-in-law Zhang was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 景初元年夏，有司議定七廟。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Jingchu the responsible officials deliberated fixing the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 (237 CE) officials debated the arrangement of the seven imperial temples.

sentences.zh: 冬，又奏曰：「蓋帝王之興，既有受命之君，又有聖妃協於神靈，然後克昌厥世，以成王業焉。

translations.literal: In winter they again submitted: "The rise of an emperor and king always has both the lord who receives the mandate and the sagely consort who harmonizes with the spirits; only then can his age flourish and the royal enterprise be completed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they memorialized: “Every dynastic founder has both the ruler who receives the mandate and the consort who answers heaven; only then does the house flourish and the great work stand complete.

sentences.zh: 昔高辛氏卜其四妃之子皆有天下，而帝摯、陶唐、商、周代興。

translations.literal: In antiquity Gaoxin divined among the sons of his four consorts and each possessed the realm, while Di Zhi, Tao Tang, Shang, and Zhou rose in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, Gaoxin divined that the sons of his four consorts would all possess all under Heaven; Di Zhi, Tao Tang, Shang, and the Zhou dynasty rose in succession.

sentences.zh: 週人上推后稷，以配皇天，追述王初，本之姜嫄，特立宮廟，世世享嘗，周禮所謂『奏夷則，歌中呂，舞大濩，以享先妣』者也。

translations.literal: The Zhou people traced their line to Hou Ji to match August Heaven; pursuing the kingly beginning to its root in Jiang Yuan they established a separate palace temple, generation after generation enjoying sacrifice—what the Rites of Zhou calls 'performing the yi mode, singing the zhong lü mode, dancing the Great Hu to honor the first mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou looked back to Hou Ji to pair with High Heaven and, tracing their kings to Jiang Yuan, set her a special temple where each generation offered sacrifice—what the Rites of Zhou means by honoring the founding mother with music and dance.

sentences.zh: 詩人頌之曰：『厥初生民，時維姜嫄。』

translations.literal: The poets praise it, saying, 'The first birth of the people—this was Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes sing, “The birth of the people began from Jiang Yuan.”

sentences.zh: 言王化之本，生民所由。

translations.literal: It speaks of the root of kingly transformation and the source from which the people come.
translations.idiomatic: That is the taproot of royal civilizing power and of the people themselves.

sentences.zh: 又曰：『閟宮有侐，實實枚枚，赫赫姜嫄，其德不回。』

translations.literal: It also says, 'The temple of Bi is solemn; truly solid, truly thick; splendidly august is Jiang Yuan, whose virtue does not waver.
translations.idiomatic: They add, “Bi’s shrine stands in awe, firm and ample; august Jiang Yuan’s virtue never falters.”

sentences.zh: 詩、禮所稱姬宗之盛，其美如此。

translations.literal: What the Odes and Rites praise of the Ji clan’s splendor is thus beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: So the canonical texts glorify the Ji house.

sentences.zh: 大魏期運，繼於有虞，然崇弘帝道，三世彌隆，廟祧之數，實與周同。

translations.literal: Great Wei’s allotted fortune succeeds that of Youyu, yet in exalting the imperial way three reigns have grown ever more glorious; the number of temples to be shifted matches Zhou’s.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s mandate follows Shun’s line, yet across three reigns the imperial way has only deepened; the temple shifts now contemplated mirror Zhou practice.

sentences.zh: 今武宣皇后、文德皇后各配無窮之祚，至於文昭皇后膺天靈符，誕育明聖​​，功濟生民，德盈宇宙，開諸後嗣，乃道化之所興也。

translations.literal: Now Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan and Empress Wen-De each match an endless blessing; as for Empress Wen-Zhao, she received heaven’s talisman, bore the enlightened sage, aided the living people, filled the cosmos with virtue, and opened the way for later heirs—she is what the transforming way exalts.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses Dowager Wu-Xuan and Wen-De already receive perpetual pairing rites; Empress Wen-Zhao bore the sage heir, succored the people, and filled heaven and earth with merit—she is the mother in whom the moral order itself is renewed.

sentences.zh: 寢廟特祀，亦姜嫄之閟宮也，而未著不毀之制，懼論功報德之義，萬世或闕焉，非所以昭孝示後世也。

translations.literal: A separate temple sacrifice is also like Jiang Yuan’s temple of Bi, yet the system of non-destruction has not been clarified; I fear the meaning of repaying merit and virtue may across myriad ages sometimes be wanting—this is not how to display filial piety and show later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Her shrine deserves singular rites like Jiang Yuan’s, yet we have not fixed the rule that her temple never be dismantled; I fear posterity might slight the duty to repay her deeds. That would ill serve filial display for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 文昭廟宜世世享祀奏樂，與祖廟同，永著不毀之典，以播聖善之風。」

translations.literal: The temple of Empress Wen-Zhao should receive sacrifice with music performed generation after generation, the same as the ancestor temples; eternally establish the norm of non-destruction, so as to spread the wind of sagely goodness."
translations.idiomatic: Wen-Zhao’s temple ought to receive music and offerings in every generation on the same footing as the founding shrines, fixing forever the rule that it never be dismantled so her sanctity may shine for ages.”

sentences.zh: 於是與七廟議並勒金策，藏之金匱。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with the deliberation on the seven temples it was inscribed on a golden document and stored in a golden coffer.
translations.idiomatic: The court then had this, together with the seven-temples decision, engraved on gold slips and laid them in the golden coffer.

sentences.zh: 帝思念舅氏不已。

translations.literal: The emperor thought of his maternal kin without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not stop thinking of his maternal kin.

sentences.zh: 暢尚幼，景初末，以暢為射聲校尉，加散騎常侍，又特為起大第，車駕親自臨之。

translations.literal: Chang was still young; at the end of Jingchu he was made Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound and additionally Regular Attendant; a great mansion was specially built for him, and the imperial carriage personally visited it.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was still young. At the end of Jingchu he was made Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound and Regular Attendant. A great mansion was specially built for him, and the emperor personally visited it.

sentences.zh: 又於其后園為像母起觀廟，名其里曰渭陽里，以追思母氏也。

translations.literal: Also in the empress's rear garden a viewing temple was built for Xiang's mother; the lane was named Weiyang Lane, to recall and think of the maternal clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the empress's rear garden a viewing temple was also built for Xiang's mother. The lane was named Weiyang Lane in remembrance of the maternal clan.

sentences.zh: 嘉平三年251年正月，暢薨，追贈車騎將軍，諡曰恭侯；

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jiaping (251 CE), Chang died; posthumously he was granted General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the posthumous title Marquis Gong;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiaping 3 (251 CE), Chang died. He was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the posthumous title Marquis Gong;

sentences.zh: 子紹嗣。

translations.literal: his son Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: his son Shao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，明帝愛女淑薨，追封諡淑為平原懿公主，為之立廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, Ming-di's beloved daughter Shu died; posthumously she was enfeoffed and titled Princess Yi of Pingyuan, and a temple was built for her.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6, Ming-di's beloved daughter Shu died. She was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess Yi of Pingyuan, and a temple was built for her.

sentences.zh: 取后亡從孫黃與合葬，追封黃列侯，以夫人郭氏從弟德為之後，承甄氏姓，封德為平原侯，襲公主爵。

translations.literal: The empress's deceased grandnephew Huang was taken to be buried with her; Huang was posthumously enfeoffed as a full marquis; Lady Guo's younger cousin De was made his heir, took the Zhen surname, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyuan, and inherited the princess's title.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's deceased grandnephew Huang was buried with her and posthumously enfeoffed as a full marquis. Lady Guo's younger cousin De was made his heir, took the Zhen surname, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyuan, and inherited the princess's title.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：於禮，婦人既無封爵之典，況於孩末，而可建以大邑乎？

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: By ritual, women already have no norm of enfeoffment and titles—how much less a child in infancy; could one establish a great fief for such a case?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng said: "By ritual, women have no norm of enfeoffment and titles. How much less an infant child—could one establish a great fief in such a case?"

sentences.zh: 德自異族，援繼非類，匪功匪親，而襲母爵，違情背典，於此為甚。

translations.literal: De came from a different clan; to pull in and continue an unsuitable line, neither by merit nor by kinship, yet to inherit a mother's title—this violates feeling and turns against the canon; in this matter the offense is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: De came from a different clan. To install him as heir without merit or kinship, yet have him inherit a mother's title, violates both feeling and canon—and here the offense was extreme.

sentences.zh: 陳群雖抗言，楊阜引事比並，然皆不能極陳先王之禮，明封建繼嗣之義，忠至之辭，猶有闕乎！

translations.literal: Although Chen Qun spoke out boldly and Yang Fu cited parallel cases, neither could fully set forth the rites of the former kings or clarify the meaning of enfeoffment and succession; their words of utmost loyalty still had gaps!
translations.idiomatic: Although Chen Qun spoke out boldly and Yang Fu cited parallel cases, neither fully set forth the rites of the former kings or clarified the meaning of enfeoffment and succession. Even their most loyal remonstrance left something unsaid!

sentences.zh: 詩云：「赫赫師尹，民具爾瞻。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Splendid is the master minister; the people all look to you."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Splendid is the master minister; the people all look to you."

sentences.zh: 宰輔之職，其可略哉！

translations.literal: The duty of chief ministers—can it be treated lightly!
translations.idiomatic: The duty of chief ministers—can it be treated lightly!

sentences.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：德字彥孫。

translations.literal: Accounts of the Lords of Jin says: De's style was Yansun.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts of the Lords of Jin says De's style was Yansun.

sentences.zh: 司馬景王輔政，以女妻德。

translations.literal: When Sima Jingwang held regency, he gave his daughter to De in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jingwang held regency, he gave his daughter to De in marriage.

sentences.zh: 妻早亡，文王復以女繼室，即京兆長公主。

translations.literal: The wife died early; King Wen again gave a daughter as a successor wife, namely the Princess Chang of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the wife died early, King Wen again gave a daughter as a successor wife—the Princess Chang of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 景、文二王欲自結於郭后，是以頻繁為婚。

translations.literal: The two kings Jing and Wen wished to bind themselves to Empress Guo, and therefore repeatedly contracted marriages.
translations.idiomatic: The two kings Jing and Wen wished to bind themselves to Empress Guo, and therefore repeatedly contracted marriages.

sentences.zh: 德雖無才學，而恭謹謙順。

translations.literal: Although De had no talent or learning, he was reverent, careful, modest, and compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Although De had no talent or learning, he was reverent, careful, modest, and compliant.

sentences.zh: 甄溫字仲舒，與郭建及德等皆后族，以事宜見寵。

translations.literal: Zhen Wen's style was Zhongshu; he, Guo Jian, De, and the rest were all empress kin and were favored for affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Wen's style was Zhongshu. He, Guo Jian, De, and the rest were all empress kin and were favored for affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 咸熙初，封郭建為臨渭縣公，德廣安縣公，邑皆千八百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianxi, Guo Jian was enfeoffed as Duke of Linwei County and De as Duke of Guang'an County, each with eighteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianxi, Guo Jian was enfeoffed as Duke of Linwei County and Guo De as Duke of Guang'an County; each fief comprised eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 溫本國侯，進為輔國大將軍，加侍中，領射聲校尉，德鎮軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Wen was originally a marquis of the founding state; he was advanced to General Who Assists the State, additionally made Palace Attendant, and put in charge as Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound; De was made General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was originally a marquis of the founding state. He was advanced to General Who Assists the State, additionally made Palace Attendant, and put in charge as Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound. De was made General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年，晉受禪，加建、德、溫三人位特進。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi, when Jin received the abdication, Jian, De, and Wen were all advanced to Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taishi, when Jin received the abdication, Jian, De, and Wen were all advanced to Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 德為人貞素，加以世祖姊夫，是以遂貴當世。

translations.literal: De as a man was upright and plain; added to this, he was the brother-in-law of Shizu, and therefore came to be honored in his age.
translations.idiomatic: De was upright and plain by nature, and as the brother-in-law of Shizu he came to be honored in his age.

sentences.zh: 德暮年官更轉為宗正，遷侍中。

translations.literal: In De's later years his office was changed to Director of the Imperial Clan, and he was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In De's later years he was made Director of the Imperial Clan and transferred to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太康中，大司馬齊王攸當之籓，德與左衛將軍王濟共諫請，時人嘉之。

translations.literal: In Taikang, when Grand Marshal Prince of Qi You was about to go to his fief, De and Left Guard General Wang Ji jointly remonstrated and petitioned; men of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang, when Grand Marshal Prince of Qi You was about to go to his fief, De and Left Guard General Wang Ji jointly remonstrated and petitioned, and men of the time praised them.

sentences.zh: 世祖以此望德，由此出德為大鴻臚，加侍中、光祿大夫，尋疾薨，贈中軍大將軍，開府侍中如故，諡恭公，子喜嗣。

translations.literal: Shizu on this account looked askance at De; for this reason De was sent out as Grand Herald, additionally made Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; soon he died of illness; posthumously he was granted General of the Central Army, with an office and Palace Attendant as before, given the posthumous title Duke Gong, and his son Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu on this account looked askance at De and sent him out as Grand Herald, additionally making him Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. Soon he died of illness. He was posthumously made General of the Central Army with an office and Palace Attendant as before, given the posthumous title Duke Gong, and his son Xi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 喜精粹有器美，歷中書郎、右衛將軍、侍中，位至輔國大將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Xi was refined and possessed fine capacity; he passed through Palace Secretary, Right Guard General, and Palace Attendant, reaching the rank of General Who Assists the State and additionally Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was refined and possessed fine capacity. He served as Palace Secretary, Right Guard General, and Palace Attendant, reaching the rank of General Who Assists the State and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 喜與國姻親，而經趙王倫、齊王冏事故，能不豫際會，良由其才短，然亦以退靜免之。

translations.literal: Xi was related by marriage to the state, yet through the affairs of Prince of Zhao Lun and Prince of Qi Jiong he was able not to take part in those encounters—likely because his talent was short, yet he was also spared by retiring into quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was related by marriage to the state, yet through the affairs of Prince of Zhao Lun and Prince of Qi Jiong he was able to stay out of those encounters—likely because his talent was limited, but also because retiring into quiet spared him.

sentences.zh: 青龍中，又封后從兄子毅及像弟三人，皆為列侯。

translations.literal: In Qinglong, the empress's cousin's son Yi and Xiang's three younger brothers were again enfeoffed, all as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong, the empress's cousin's son Yi and Xiang's three younger brothers were again enfeoffed, all as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 毅數上疏陳時政，官至越騎校尉。

translations.literal: Yi repeatedly submitted memorials setting forth current policy and reached the office of Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yi repeatedly submitted memorials on current policy and reached the office of Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 嘉平中，复封暢子二人為列侯。

translations.literal: In Jiaping, Chang's two sons were again enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaping, Chang's two sons were again enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 后兄儼孫女為齊王皇后，后父已沒，封后母為廣樂鄉君。

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Yan's granddaughter became empress to the Prince of Qi; the empress's father was already dead, so the empress's mother was enfeoffed as Lady of Guangle Township.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's elder brother Yan's granddaughter became empress to the Prince of Qi. The empress's father was already dead, so her mother was enfeoffed as Lady of Guangle Township.

sentences.zh: 文德郭皇后，安平廣宗人也。

translations.literal: Empress Wen-De, née Guo, was a native of Guangzong in Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen-De of the Guo clan came from Guangzong in Anping.

sentences.zh: 祖世長吏。

translations.literal: For generations her forebears were chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: For generations her forebears had served as chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：父永，官至南郡太守，諡敬侯。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei says: her father Yong reached the office of Administrator of Nan Commandery and was given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says her father Yong reached the office of Administrator of Nan Commandery and received the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 母姓董氏，即堂陽君，生三男二女：長男浮，高唐令，次女昱，次即后，后弟都，弟成。

translations.literal: Her mother was of the Dong clan, namely Lady Tangyang; she bore three sons and two daughters: the eldest son Fu, Magistrate of Gaotang; the second daughter Yu; next was the empress; the empress's younger brothers Du and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was of the Dong clan, namely Lady Tangyang. She bore three sons and two daughters: the eldest son Fu, Magistrate of Gaotang; the second daughter Yu; next the empress; and the empress's younger brothers Du and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 后以漢中平元年三月乙卯生，生而有異常。

translations.literal: The empress was born on the yimao day of the third month of the first year of Zhongping of Han; at birth there were unusual signs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was born on the yimao day of the third month of Han Zhongping 1; at birth there were unusual signs.

sentences.zh: 后少而父永奇之曰：「此乃吾女中王也。」

translations.literal: When the empress was young her father Yong marveled at her, saying, "This is the king among my daughters."
translations.idiomatic: When the empress was young her father Yong marveled at her, saying, "This is the king among my daughters."

sentences.zh: 遂以女王為字。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Nüwang as her style.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he took Nüwang as her style.

sentences.zh: 早失二親，喪亂流離，沒在銅鞮侯家。

translations.literal: She early lost both parents; in the chaos of mourning and disorder she was cast adrift and ended up in the household of the Marquis of Tongdi.
translations.idiomatic: She early lost both parents. In the chaos of war and exile she ended up in the household of the Marquis of Tongdi.

sentences.zh: 太祖為魏公時，得入東宮。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor became Duke of Wei, she was able to enter the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor became Duke of Wei, she entered the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 后有智數，時時有所獻納。

translations.literal: The empress had wisdom and calculation and from time to time offered suggestions.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was clever and from time to time offered suggestions.

sentences.zh: 文帝定為嗣，后有謀焉。

translations.literal: When Wen-di was fixed as heir, the empress had a hand in the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen-di was fixed as heir, the empress had a hand in the plan.

sentences.zh: 太子即王位，后為夫人，及踐阼，為貴嬪。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent took the royal title, the empress became Lady; when he ascended the throne, she became Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent took the royal title, she became Lady; when he ascended the throne, she became Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 甄后之死，由后之寵也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhen's death came from this empress's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhen's death came from this empress's favor.

sentences.zh: 黃初三年，將登后位，文帝欲立為后，中郎棧潛上疏曰：「在昔帝王之治天下，不惟外輔，亦有內助，治亂所由，盛衰從之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu, as she was about to ascend the empress's seat, Wen-di wished to install her as empress; Palace Gentleman Stack Qian submitted a memorial, saying, "In former times when emperors and kings governed the realm, they relied not only on outer assistance but also on inner support; order and disorder arise from this, and rise and decline follow it.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3, as she was about to ascend the empress's seat, Wen-di wished to install her as empress. Palace Gentleman Stack Qian submitted a memorial, saying, "In former times when emperors and kings governed the realm, they relied not only on outer assistance but also on inner support; order and disorder arise from this, and rise and decline follow it.

sentences.zh: 故西陵配黃，英娥降媯，並以賢明，流芳上世。

translations.literal: Therefore Xiling was paired with Huang and the heroic maid descended to the Gui clan; all by sage wisdom and clarity, their fragrance flowed in upper ages.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Xiling was paired with Huang and the heroic maid descended to the Gui clan—all by sage wisdom and clarity, their fame flowed through upper ages.

sentences.zh: 桀奔南巢，禍階末喜；

translations.literal: Jie fled to Southern Nest and disaster began with Mo Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Jie fled to Southern Nest and disaster began with Mo Xi;

sentences.zh: 紂以砲烙，怡悅妲己。

translations.literal: Zhou used the burning pillar and took delight in Daji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou used the burning pillar and took delight in Daji.

sentences.zh: 是以聖哲慎立元妃，必取先代世族之家，擇其令淑以統六宮，虔奉宗廟，陰教聿修。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage and wise are careful in establishing the primary consort; they must take a house of hereditary clans of former ages, choose one who is good and virtuous to govern the six palaces, reverently serve the ancestral temple, and fully cultivate inner instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage and wise are careful in establishing the primary consort. They must take a house of hereditary clans of former ages, choose one who is good and virtuous to govern the six palaces, reverently serve the ancestral temple, and fully cultivate inner instruction.

sentences.zh: 易曰：『家道正而天下定。』

translations.literal: The Changes says, 'When the way of the family is correct, the realm is settled.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "When the way of the family is correct, the realm is settled."

sentences.zh: 由內及外，先王之令典也。

translations.literal: From inner to outer—this is the august norm of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: From inner to outer—this is the august norm of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 春秋書宗人釁夏云，無以妾為夫人之禮。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn records the Director of the Clan performing the summer offering and says there is no rite for making a concubine a lady.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn records the clan officer Xin Xia and shows that there is no ritual basis for making a concubine into the principal lady.

sentences.zh: 齊桓誓命於葵丘，亦曰『無以妾為妻』。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi swore his command at Kuqiu and likewise said, 'Do not take a concubine as wife.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi swore his command at Kuqiu and likewise said, "Do not take a concubine as wife."

sentences.zh: 今后宮嬖寵，常亞乘輿。

translations.literal: Now in the inner palace favored concubines often rank just below the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the inner palace favored concubines often rank just below the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 若因愛登后，使賤人暴貴，臣恐後世下陵上替，開張非度，亂自上起也。」

translations.literal: If through affection one installs her as empress and makes a base person suddenly exalted, I fear that in later ages inferiors will encroach on superiors and the proper order will be overturned, irregular practices will be opened wide, and disorder will rise from above."
translations.idiomatic: If through affection one installs her as empress and makes a base person suddenly exalted, I fear that in later ages inferiors will encroach on superiors, irregular practices will be opened wide, and disorder will rise from above."

sentences.zh: 文帝不從，遂立為皇后。

translations.literal: Wen-di did not follow this and thereupon installed her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wen-di did not follow this and installed her as empress.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：后上表謝曰：「妾無皇、英釐降之節，又非姜、任思齊之倫，誠不足以假充女君之盛位，處中饋之重任。」

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: the empress submitted a memorial of thanks, saying, "Your handmaid lacks the virtue of Huang and Ying or the descending grace of Li; nor am I of the same order as Jiang and Ren in aspiring to equal virtue. Truly I am not sufficient to borrow and fill the exalted seat of the female sovereign or bear the heavy charge of the inner kitchen."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says the empress submitted a memorial of thanks, saying, "Your handmaid lacks the virtue of Huang and Ying or the descending grace of Li, nor am I of the same order as Jiang and Ren in aspiring to equal virtue. Truly I am not fit to fill the exalted seat of the female sovereign or bear the heavy charge of the inner household."

sentences.zh: 后自在東宮，及即尊位，雖有異寵，心愈恭肅，供養永壽宮，以孝聞。

translations.literal: From the time she was in the Eastern Palace until she reached the honored position, although she had special favor, her heart grew ever more reverent and solemn; she supported Yongshou Palace and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: From the Eastern Palace until she reached the honored position, although she had special favor, her heart grew ever more reverent and solemn. She supported Yongshou Palace and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 是時柴貴人亦有寵，后教訓獎導之。

translations.literal: At that time Honored Lady Chai also had favor; the empress instructed, exhorted, and guided her.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Honored Lady Chai also had favor, and the empress instructed, exhorted, and guided her.

sentences.zh: 后宮諸貴人時有過失，常彌覆之，有譴讓，輒為帝言其本末，帝或大有所怒，至為之頓首請罪，是以六宮無怨。

translations.literal: When the various honored ladies of the inner palace at times had faults, she constantly covered them over; when there was reproof or censure, she would explain the whole matter to the emperor; the emperor might become greatly angry, even to the point that she would kowtow and plead guilt—thus the six palaces were without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When the various honored ladies of the inner palace at times had faults, she constantly covered them over. When there was reproof or censure, she would explain the whole matter to the emperor. The emperor might become greatly angry, even to the point that she would kowtow and plead guilt—thus the six palaces were without resentment.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，不好音樂，常慕漢明德馬后之為人。

translations.literal: By nature she was frugal and restrained, disliked music, and constantly admired the conduct of Empress Ma the Bright and Virtuous of Han.
translations.idiomatic: By nature she was frugal and restrained, disliked music, and constantly admired the conduct of Empress Ma the Bright and Virtuous of Han.

sentences.zh: 后早喪兄弟，以從兄表繼永後，拜奉車都尉。

translations.literal: The empress had early lost her brothers; she took her cousin Biao to continue Yong’s posterity and invested him as Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: After her brothers died young, she had her cousin Guo Biao posthumously continue another brother’s line and appointed him commandant of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 后外親劉斐與他國為婚，后聞之，敕曰：「諸親戚嫁娶，自當與鄉里門戶匹敵者，不得因勢，強與他方人婚也。」

translations.literal: When an outer kinsman of the empress, Liu Fei, contracted a marriage with another state, the empress heard of it and instructed, saying, "In the marriages of our kin they naturally ought to match families of comparable standing in their own villages and gates; they must not rely on power to force unions with people from distant regions."
translations.idiomatic: When a relative by marriage, Liu Fei, allied his house with another kingdom, she issued an order: “Our kinsmen’s weddings should pair like with like in their own neighborhoods; no one may use influence to drag in spouses from far away.”

sentences.zh: 后姊子孟武還鄉里，求小妻，后止之。

translations.literal: Her elder sister’s son Meng Wu returned to his home region seeking a concubine; the empress stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: She also blocked her sister’s son Meng Wu when he went home looking for a secondary wife.

sentences.zh: 遂敕諸家曰：「今世婦女少，當配將士，不得因緣取以為妾也。

translations.literal: Thereupon she instructed the various families, saying, "In the present age women are few; they ought to be given in marriage to soldiers and officers; you must not seize pretexts to take them as concubines.
translations.idiomatic: She then warned every branch of the clan: “Women are scarce in wartime; they belong with the troops. Do not invent excuses to press them into concubinage.

sentences.zh: 宜各自慎，無為罰首。」

translations.literal: Each should be cautious on his own account and not be the first to incur punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Watch yourselves—do not be the first to bring down the law.”

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：后常敕戒表、武等曰：「漢氏椒房之家，少能自全者，皆由驕奢，可不慎乎！」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: The empress often admonished Biao, Wu, and the like, saying, "Among the pepper-chamber houses of Han, few could preserve themselves—all because of arrogance and extravagance; can one not be cautious!"〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Book of Wei adds that she repeatedly cautioned Guo Biao, Meng Wu, and their circle: “Few consort clans under Han survived their own pride and waste—take care.”〉

sentences.zh: 五年，帝東征，后留許昌永始台。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor campaigned east; the empress remained at Yongshi Terrace in Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of an era (Huangchu) the emperor marched east while she stayed at Yongshi Terrace in Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 時霖雨百餘日，城樓多壞，有司奏請移止。

translations.literal: At that time there was unbroken rain for more than a hundred days; many city towers were damaged, and the responsible officials memorialized asking to move her lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell for over a hundred days straight, ruining tower works, so officials begged her to relocate.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「昔楚昭王出遊，貞姜留漸台，江水至，使者迎而無符，不去，卒沒。

translations.literal: The empress said, "In antiquity when King Zhao of Chu traveled abroad, the chaste Lady Jiang remained on the Gradual Terrace; when the river rose the messenger came to fetch her but lacked the tally, so she would not leave and at last drowned.
translations.idiomatic: She answered, “Long ago, when King Zhao of Chu was away, his faithful Jiang stayed on the Gradual Terrace; the river rose, yet without the proper tally she refused to flee and drowned.

sentences.zh: 今帝在遠，吾幸未有是患，而便移止，奈何？」

translations.literal: Now the emperor is far away; I have fortunately not yet met with that calamity—yet I should move lodging—how could that be right?"
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is far off, and I have no such flood at my door—why should I bolt at the first leak?”

sentences.zh: 群臣莫敢復言。

translations.literal: None of the ministers dared speak again.
translations.idiomatic: No minister dared press the point again.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝東征吳，至廣陵，后留譙宮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor campaigned east against Wu, reaching Guangling; the empress remained at the palace in Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he campaigned east against Wu as far as Guangling, leaving her at the Qiao palace.

sentences.zh: 時表留宿衛，欲遏水取魚。

translations.literal: At that time Biao remained on night guard and wished to dam water to catch fish.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Biao, left on night duty, wanted to block a stream to seine for fish.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「水噹通運漕，又少材木，奴客不在目前，當複私取官竹木作梁遏。

translations.literal: The empress said, "The water ought to remain open for the transport canal; moreover timber is scarce; the slaves and retainers are not before one’s eyes—would one again privately take official bamboo and timber to make beams for a dam?
translations.idiomatic: She reproved him: “That water feeds the supply barges, and lumber is short. Your servants are not here to haul timber—would you raid government bamboo to brace a private weir?

sentences.zh: 今奉車所不足者，豈魚乎？」

translations.literal: What the commandant of the carriage lacks—is it fish?"
translations.idiomatic: Is the commandant of the carriage short of fish?”

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，尊后為皇太后，稱永安宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne he honored the empress as Empress Dowager, with her residence called Yong'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming-di succeeded he raised the empress to Empress Dowager of Yong'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，詔封表安陽亭侯，又進爵鄉侯，增邑並前五百戶，遷中壘將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe an edict enfeoffed Biao as Marquis of Anyang Pavilion, then advanced his rank to village marquis, added five hundred households to his fief together with what he already held, and transferred him to General of the Central Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4 an edict made Guo Biao Marquis of Anyang Pavilion, then promoted him to village marquis, added five hundred households to his fief for a total with prior holdings, and appointed him general of the central rampart.

sentences.zh: 以表子詳為騎都尉。

translations.literal: He appointed Biao's son Xiang as Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He made Biao's son Guo Xiang cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 其年，帝追諡太后父永為安陽鄉敬侯，母董為都鄉君。

translations.literal: That year the emperor posthumously honored the empress dowager's father Yong as Marquis Jing of Anyang Village and her mother Dong as Mistress of the Capital Village.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the emperor posthumously ennobled the empress dowager's father Yong as Marquis Jing of Anyang village and her mother Dong as lady of the capital village.

sentences.zh: 遷表昭德將軍，加金紫，位特進，表第二子訓為騎都尉。

translations.literal: Biao was transferred to General Who Displays Virtue, given the gold seal and purple ribbon, granted the position of Special Advance, and Biao's second son Xun was made Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Biao was promoted to general who displays virtue, given the gold seal and purple cord and the rank of special advance; Biao's second son Xun became cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 及孟武母卒，欲厚葬，起祠堂，太后止之曰：「自喪亂以來，墳墓無不發掘，皆由厚葬也；

translations.literal: When Meng Wu's mother died and he wished a lavish burial and to erect an ancestral hall, the empress dowager stopped him, saying, "Since the disorders of war, tombs have all been opened and plundered—all because of lavish burial;
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Wu's mother died and he wanted a lavish funeral and an ancestral shrine, the empress dowager forbade it, saying, "Since the age of chaos no tomb has escaped looting, and lavish burial is always the reason;

sentences.zh: 首陽陵可以為法。」

translations.literal: Shouyang Mausoleum may serve as the model."
translations.idiomatic: Take Shouyang Mausoleum as your model."

sentences.zh: 青龍三年春，后崩於許昌，以終制營陵，三月庚寅，葬首陽陵西。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Qinglong the empress dowager died at Xuchang; following the final rites a mausoleum was built, and on gengyin in the third month she was buried west of Shouyang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qinglong 3 the empress dowager died at Xuchang. A tomb was built according to the prescribed mourning rites, and on gengyin of the third month she was buried west of Shouyang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：明帝既嗣立，追痛甄后之薨，故太后以憂暴崩。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: Once Emperor Ming had succeeded to the throne and grieved anew for Empress Zhen's death, the empress dowager therefore died suddenly from distress.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that once Emperor Ming had succeeded to the throne and grieved anew over Empress Zhen's death, the empress dowager therefore died suddenly from distress.

sentences.zh: 甄后臨沒，以帝屬李夫人。

translations.literal: When Empress Zhen was near death she entrusted the emperor to Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: As Empress Wen-Zhao lay dying she entrusted the emperor to Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，夫人乃說甄后見譖之禍，不獲大斂，被髮覆面，帝哀恨流涕，命殯葬太后，皆如甄后故事。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died Lady Li then told how Empress Zhen had suffered slander and calamity, had not received full encoffinment, and had been left with hair loose and face covered; the emperor mourned and wept in bitter regret and ordered that the empress dowager's funeral and burial follow Empress Zhen's precedent in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, Lady Li recounted how Empress Wen-Zhao had been slandered to her ruin, denied proper encoffinment, and left with hair loose over her face. The emperor wept in grief and rage and ordered the empress dowager's funeral handled exactly as Empress Wen-Zhao's had been.

sentences.zh: 漢晉春秋曰：初，甄后之誅，由郭后之寵，及殯，令被髮覆面，以糠塞口，遂立郭后，使養明帝。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin states: At first Empress Zhen's execution came from Empress Guo's favor; at the encoffinment she was made to let her hair hang and cover her face, with chaff stuffed in her mouth; then Empress Guo was established and made to rear Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says that Empress Zhen's execution originally came from Empress Guo's favor; when she was encoffined, she was made to wear her hair loose over her face, with chaff stuffed in her mouth. Empress Guo was then established and made to raise Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，心常懷忿，數泣問甄后死狀。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this and constantly harbored resentment, weeping again and again as he asked how Empress Zhen had died.
translations.idiomatic: Ming-di knew this and nursed a lasting grievance, weeping repeatedly as he questioned how Empress Wen-Zhao had died.

sentences.zh: 郭后曰：「先帝自殺，何以責問我？

translations.literal: Empress Guo said, "The former emperor killed himself—why do you hold me to account?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen-De answered, "The late emperor took his own life—why blame me?

sentences.zh: 且汝為人子，可追讎死父，為前母枉殺後母邪？」

translations.literal: Moreover, as a son, can you pursue vengeance for a dead father and wrongly kill your stepmother for your former mother?"
translations.idiomatic: And as his son, would you avenge a dead father by killing your stepmother for your birth mother's sake?"

sentences.zh: 明帝怒，遂逼殺之，敕殯者使如甄后故事。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming grew angry, then forced her to death, and instructed those handling the encoffinment to follow Empress Zhen's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Ming-di flew into a rage, forced her to her death, and ordered the embalmers to treat her exactly as Empress Wen-Zhao had been treated.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》載哀策曰：「維青龍三年三月壬申，皇太后梓宮啟殯，將葬於首陽之西陵。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei records the lamentation patent, saying, "In the third year of Qinglong, on the third month, day renshen, the empress dowager's coffin was opened for encoffinment and was to be buried at the western mausoleum of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei preserves the lamentation patent: "In Qinglong 3, on renshen of the third month, the empress dowager's coffin was opened for burial at the western tomb of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 哀子皇帝叡親奉冊祖載，遂親遣奠，叩心擗踴，號咷仰訴，痛靈魂之遷幸，悲容車之向路，背三光以潛翳，就黃壚而安厝。

translations.literal: The grieving son, Emperor Rui, personally bore the patent and ancestral carriage, then personally sent forth offerings, beating his breast and stamping in grief, wailing and crying heavenward in appeal, pained that the spirit soul was being removed in favor, grieved that the bier was setting out on its road, turning his back on the three luminaries as they dimmed in concealment, and coming to the yellow mound for peaceful rest.
translations.idiomatic: The grieving son, Emperor Rui, personally bore the patent and ancestral carriage, then offered sacrifice himself—beating his breast, stamping in anguish, wailing heavenward—mourning the spirit's departure, grieving the bier's journey, turning from the sun, moon, and stars now dimmed, and committing her to the yellow earth in peace.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 昔二女妃虞，帝道以彰，三母嬪週，聖善彌光，既多受祉，享國延長。

translations.literal: In antiquity two daughters became consorts of Yu and the imperial way was thereby made manifest; three mothers entered the Zhou house and sagely goodness shone ever brighter; they received abundant blessing and their states endured long.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago two daughters wed into Yu's line and the imperial way shone forth; three mothers entered Zhou and sanctity grew ever brighter—they received great blessing and their realms endured.

sentences.zh: 哀哀慈妣，興化閏房，龍飛紫極，作合聖皇，不虞中年，暴罹災殃。

translations.literal: Mournful, mournful is my gracious mother, who raised transforming influence within the inner chambers, rose with the dragon to the purple apex, and was paired with the sage emperor—yet who did not expect mid-life and suddenly met calamity and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Mournful is my gracious mother, who nurtured virtue in the inner chambers, rose to the purple throne beside the sage emperor, and yet, in mid-life, was suddenly struck by disaster.

sentences.zh: 愍予小子，煢煢摧傷，魂雖永逝，定省曷望？

translations.literal: Pity me, this little child, lonely and broken in grief; though the soul has forever departed, how can I still hope for morning and evening attendance?
translations.idiomatic: Pity me, a lonely child crushed with grief; though her soul is gone forever, how can I ever again attend her morning and evening?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！」

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!"

sentences.zh: 帝進表爵為觀津侯，增邑五百，並前千戶。

translations.literal: The emperor advanced Biao's noble rank to Marquis of Guanjin, added five hundred households to his fief, making one thousand together with what he already held.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promoted Guo Biao to Marquis of Guanjin, added five hundred households to his fief, and brought his total holdings to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 遷詳為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Xiang was transferred to Commandant of the Stable for the Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang was made commandant of the stable for the emperor's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 四年，追改封永為觀津敬侯，世婦董為堂陽君。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Yong was posthumously re-enfeoffed as Marquis Jing of Guanjin and the late wife Dong as Mistress of Tangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yong was posthumously re-enfeoffed as Marquis Jing of Guanjin and the late wife Dong as lady of Tangyang.

sentences.zh: 追封諡后兄浮為梁裡亭戴侯，都為武城亭孝侯，成為新樂亭定侯，皆使使者奉策，祠以太牢。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffing and honoring the empress's elder brothers, Fu was made Marquis Dai of Liangli Pavilion, Du Marquis Xiao of Wucheng Pavilion, and Cheng Marquis Ding of Xinle Pavilion; envoys were sent to each bearing patents, and they were sacrificed to with the grand offering.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's brothers were posthumously ennobled: Fu as Marquis Dai of Liangli pavilion, Du as Marquis Xiao of Wucheng pavilion, and Cheng as Marquis Ding of Xinle pavilion. Envoys were dispatched with patents to sacrifice to each with the grand offering.

sentences.zh: 詳薨，子釗嗣。

translations.literal: Xiang died, and his son Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang died and was succeeded by his son Zhao.

sentences.zh: 明悼毛皇后，河內人也。

translations.literal: Empress Ming-Dao, née Mao, was a native of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao, honored as Empress Ming-Dao, came from Henei.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，以選入東宮，明帝時為平原王，進御有寵，出入與同輿輦。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era she was selected into the Eastern Palace; when Emperor Ming was Prince of Pingyuan she attended his bed and had favor, going out and in in the same carriage and palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu she was selected into the Eastern Palace; while Emperor Ming was still Prince of Pingyuan, she attended him and won favor, going in and out in the same carriage and palanquin.

sentences.zh: 及即帝立，以為貴嬪。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne and was established as emperor he made her Honored Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne he raised her to Honored Concubine.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 后父​​嘉，拜騎都尉，后弟曾，郎中。

translations.literal: The empress’s father Jia was appointed Cavalry Commandant; her younger brother Zeng, Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Mao Jia became cavalry commandant; her brother Mao Zeng, a gentleman at court.

sentences.zh: 初，明帝為王，始納河內虞氏為妃，帝即位，虞氏不得立為后，太皇后卞太后慰勉焉。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Ming was a prince, he first took Lady Yu of Henei as consort; when he ascended the throne Lady Yu could not be established as empress, and Grand Empress Dowager Bian comforted and encouraged her.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming-di was still a prince he first took Lady Yu of Henei as consort. Once he took the throne she could not be made empress, and Grand Empress Dowager Bian tried to console her.

sentences.zh: 虞氏曰：「曹氏自好立賤，未有能以義舉者也。

translations.literal: Lady Yu said, "The Cao house has always liked to elevate the base; none has ever been raised on grounds of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yu replied, "The Cao clan has always favored elevating the lowborn; none has ever been raised on grounds of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 然后職內事，君聽外政，其道相由而成，苟不能以善始，未有能令終者也。

translations.literal: Yet the empress manages inner affairs and the lord listens to outer government; their way is mutually completed thereby; if one cannot begin well, none has ever been able to finish well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the empress governs within while the sovereign rules without, and the two must work together. If the beginning is not good, the end is never good.

sentences.zh: 殆必由此亡國喪祀矣！」

translations.literal: This will surely be how the state is lost and the sacrifices cut off!"
translations.idiomatic: This is surely how a realm loses its altars and its line!"

sentences.zh: 虞氏遂絀還鄴宮。

translations.literal: Lady Yu then withdrew with a black headband and returned to the palace at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yu then put on mourning dress and withdrew to the palace at Ye.

sentences.zh: 進嘉為奉車都尉，曾騎都尉，寵賜隆渥。

translations.literal: Jia was promoted to Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and Zeng to Cavalry Commandant, with favor and gifts rich and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jia was promoted to commandant of the imperial carriage and Mao Zeng to cavalry commandant, with lavish favor and gifts.

sentences.zh: 頃之，封嘉博平鄉侯，遷光祿大夫，曾駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Before long Jia was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boping Village and transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; Zeng was made Commandant of the Stable for the Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mao Jia was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boping village and made grand master for splendid happiness; Mao Zeng became commandant of the stable for the son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 嘉本典虞車工，卒暴富貴，明帝令朝臣會其家飲宴，其容止舉動甚蚩騃，語輒自謂「侯身」，時人以為笑。

translations.literal: Jia had originally been overseer of the Yu clan's carriage craftsmen and suddenly became rich and noble; Emperor Ming ordered court ministers to gather at his home for drink and feast; his bearing and movements were very crude and foolish, and in speech he constantly called himself "this marquis's person"; people of the time took it as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: Jia had once overseen the Yu family's carriage workshops and suddenly shot to wealth and rank. Ming-di had court ministers feast at his house, where his manners were oafish and he kept calling himself "the marquis's own person"—a laughingstock at the time.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：古之王者，必求令淑以對揚至德，恢王化於關雎，致淳風於麟趾。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng states: The kings of antiquity necessarily sought worthy and virtuous consorts to respond to and display supreme virtue, extending kingly transformation through Guanju and bringing pure custom through Linzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng writes: Ancient kings sought worthy consorts to answer and display supreme virtue, spreading royal civilizing power through Guanju and pure custom through Linzhi.

sentences.zh: 及臻三季，並亂茲緒，義以情溺，位由寵昏，貴賤無章，下陵上替，興衰隆廢，皆是物也。

translations.literal: When the three later ages were reached they all disrupted this thread: righteousness drowned in emotion, rank came through favor and folly, noble and base lacked distinction, the lower encroached and the upper declined, rise and fall, flourishing and ruin—all were the same thing.
translations.idiomatic: By the three later ages that thread was ruined everywhere: duty drowned in passion, rank won through blind favor, noble and base confused, inferiors overrunning superiors—rise and fall alike followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 魏自武王，暨於烈祖，三后之升，起自幽賤，本既卑矣，何以長世？

translations.literal: From King Wu of Wei down to the Fierce Ancestor, the elevation of three empresses all began from obscure and base origins; the root was already low—how could the line endure long?
translations.idiomatic: From Cao Cao down to Cao Pi, three empresses were raised from obscure and humble origins. With so low a foundation, how could the house endure for ages?

sentences.zh: 詩云：「絺兮绤兮，淒其以風。」

translations.literal: The Odes say, "Fine and coarse linen—how chill it is in the wind."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Fine and coarse linen—how chill it is in the wind."

sentences.zh: 其此之謂乎！

translations.literal: Is this not what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not exactly what is meant!

sentences.zh: 后又加嘉位特進，曾遷散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later the empress again added for Jia the position of Special Advance, and Zeng was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress later gave Mao Jia the rank of special advance and moved Mao Zeng to attendant gentleman at court.

sentences.zh: 青龍三年，嘉薨，追贈光祿大夫，改封安國侯，增邑五百，並前千戶，諡曰節侯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qinglong Jia died; he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo, given five hundred added households making one thousand together with prior holdings, and honored with the posthumous title Marquis Jie.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 3 Mao Jia died. He was posthumously made grand master for splendid happiness, re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo with five hundred added households for a total of one thousand, and given the posthumous title Marquis Jie.

sentences.zh: 四年，追封后母夏為野王君。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the empress's mother Xia was posthumously enfeoffed as Mistress of Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the empress's mother Xia was posthumously enfeoffed as lady of Yewang.

sentences.zh: 帝之幸郭元后也，后愛寵日弛。

translations.literal: When the emperor favored Lady Guo who would be empress with the Yuan title, the empress’s love and favor daily slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ming-di’s affection shifted to Lady Guo—the future Empress Yuan—Lady Mao’s favor ebbed by the day.

sentences.zh: 景初元年，帝遊后園，召才人以上曲宴極樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu the emperor toured the rear garden and summoned concubines of Talent rank and above to a winding banquet with utmost merriment.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 he held a private revel in the rear park with every consort from Talent upward.

sentences.zh: 元后曰「宜延皇后」，帝弗許。

translations.literal: The Yuan empress said, "You ought to invite the empress"; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan empress said, "You ought to invite the empress"; the emperor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 乃禁左右，使不得宣。

translations.literal: He then silenced those around him so they could not announce it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to keep silent so word would not reach her.

sentences.zh: 后知之，明日，帝見后，后曰：「昨日遊宴北園，樂乎？」

translations.literal: When the empress learned of it, the next day when the emperor saw the empress she said, "Yesterday you feasted in the north garden—was it pleasant?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when he came to her apartments, she asked calmly, “Was the north-garden party yesterday to your liking?”

sentences.zh: 帝以左右洩之，所殺十餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor, because those at his side had leaked it, killed more than ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged that someone had told her, he executed over a dozen people.

sentences.zh: 賜后死，然猶加諡，葬愍陵。

translations.literal: He granted the empress death, yet still added a posthumous title and buried her at Min Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He then forced her to take her own life, yet still granted a posthumous name and buried her at the Mausoleum of Lament.

sentences.zh: 遷曾散騎常侍，後徙為羽林虎賁中郎將、原武典農。

translations.literal: Zeng was promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, later transferred to Colonel of the Feathered Forest Tiger Guards and Director of Agriculture for Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zeng was moved up to regular attendant at court, then to colonel of the feathered forest guards and overseer of the Yuanwu agricultural colony.

sentences.zh: 明元郭皇后，西平人也，世河右大族。

translations.literal: Empress Ming-Yuan of the Guo clan was a native of Xiping and for generations a great clan west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ming-Yuan of the Guo clan came from Xiping; her family was a great house west of the Yellow River for generations.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，本郡反叛，遂沒入宮。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era the commandery rebelled, and she was then taken into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu her commandery rebelled, and she was taken into the palace.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，甚見愛幸，拜為夫人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne she was greatly favored and invested as Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ming-di succeeded she won great favor and was made Lady.

sentences.zh: 叔父立為騎都尉，從父芝為虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Her father's younger brother Li was appointed Cavalry Commandant; her father's cousin Zhi was made Colonel of the Tiger Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle Li became cavalry commandant and her father's cousin Guo Zhi colonel of the tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 帝疾困，遂立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor was gravely ill she was then established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 齊王即位，尊后為皇太后，稱永寧宮，追封諡太后父滿為西都定侯，以立子建紹其爵。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi ascended the throne he honored her as Empress Dowager, with her residence called Yongning Palace; he posthumously enfeoffed and honored the empress dowager's father Man as Marquis Ding of Xidu, and had his son Jian continue his noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Fang succeeded he raised her to Empress Dowager of Yongning Palace, posthumously ennobled her father Man as Marquis Ding of Xidu, and had his son Jian inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 封太后母杜為郃陽君。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's mother Du was enfeoffed as Mistress of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Du was enfeoffed as lady of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 芝遷散騎常侍、長水校尉，《魏略》曰：諸郭之中，芝最壯直。

translations.literal: Zhi was transferred to Regular Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Changshui Guard; the Wei Summary states: Among all the Guo clan, Zhi was the most forceful and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi was promoted to regular palace attendant and colonel of the Changshui guard. The Wei Summary says that among the Guo clan Zhi was the most forceful and upright.

sentences.zh: 先時自以他功封侯。

translations.literal: Earlier he had on other merit been enfeoffed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier been enfeoffed as marquis on other merits.

sentences.zh: 立，宣德將軍，皆封列侯。

translations.literal: Li was made General Who Displays Virtue; both were enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Li was made general who displays virtue; both were enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 建兄德，出養甄氏。

translations.literal: Jian's elder brother De had been given out in adoption to the Zhen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's elder brother De had been given in adoption to the Zhen clan.

sentences.zh: 德及建俱為鎮護將軍，皆封列侯，並掌宿衛。

translations.literal: De and Jian were both made Generals Who Guard the Garrisons, all enfeoffed as full marquises, and together held command of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: De and Jian both became generals who guard the garrisons, were enfeoffed as full marquises, and jointly commanded the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 值三主幼弱，宰輔統政，與奪大事，皆先諮啟於太后而後施行。

translations.literal: It happened that three rulers were young and weak and chief ministers held unified government; in granting and taking away great affairs all first consulted and reported to the empress dowager and only then were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: With three successive child emperors and regents holding power, every major appointment or dismissal was first reported to the empress dowager before it was enacted.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉、鍾會等作亂，咸假其命而以為辭焉。

translations.literal: When Guanqiu Jian, Zhong Hui, and others raised rebellion, they all borrowed her command and used it as their pretext.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian, Zhong Hui, and others rebelled, they all invoked her authority as their pretext.

sentences.zh: 景元四年十二日崩，五年二月，葬高平陵西。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Jingyuan she died; in the second month of the fifth year she was buried west of Gaoping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the twelfth month of Jingyuan 4 and was buried west of Gaoping Mausoleum in the second month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：建字叔始，有器局而強問，泰始中疾薨。

translations.literal: Commendations of the Lords of Jin states: Jian, courtesy name Shushi, had capacity and breadth of vision and was forceful in inquiry; in the Taishi era he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Commendations of the Lords of Jin records that Jian, styled Shushi, had breadth of vision and forceful judgment; he died of illness during Taishi.

sentences.zh: 子嘏嗣，為給事中。

translations.literal: His son Gu succeeded and served as Supervisor in Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu succeeded him and served as supervisor in attendance.

translations.literal: 【Commentary】
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 評曰：魏后妃之家，雖云富貴，未有若衰漢乘非其據，宰割朝政者也。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Among the families of Wei’s empresses and consorts, though they are called rich and noble, none seized illegitimate position and carved up court government as did the declining Han.
translations.idiomatic: The historian’s verdict: Wei’s consort clans grew wealthy, yet none usurped the government the way late Han favorites did.

sentences.zh: 鑑往易軌，於斯為美。

translations.literal: Taking the past as a mirror and changing the track—herein lies the good.
translations.idiomatic: They learned from history and kept to a safer path—that is the virtue here.

sentences.zh: 追觀陳群之議，棧潛之論，適足以為百王之規典，垂憲範乎後葉矣。

translations.literal: Looking back at Chen Qun’s memorial and Zhan Qian’s discourse, they suffice to be a normative model for a hundred kings and to hang a legal pattern before later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in hindsight, Chen Qun’s memorial and Zhan Qian’s admonitions are enough to serve as precedent for any line of kings and to hand down a pattern of law for generations yet to come.
